still blocking, and the named lead is now exhausted at the cape depot. the queue pointed at the estate papers of his wife magdelena elisabeth de beer, d. 1843. the cape town archives repository has been searched under de beer + magdelena, beer + magdelena + elisabeth, booysen + magdelena, booijsen + magdelena, booysen + gerthardus, booysen + gerhardus, booyzen + gerhardus and booysen + lodewikus/lodewicus. there is no estate file for her, and none for him. one near-miss worth recording and not adopting: kab ncd 2/1: 49, a notarial will of 1793 for 'jan booysen, married to the late magdalena de beer' — wrong husband's name, and a wife already dead fifty years before ours. it shows booysen–de beer was not a unique pairing, which is a warning about the tree rather than a lead. what has changed, 10 september 2026: the 1876 rustenburg sterfkennis of his son now names both of them in line 3 — "gerthardus lödewikus booijsen" and "magdalena de beer". that does not answer this question, which is about his parents, and the entry stays blocking. but generation seven is no longer an assertion of the family tree, the 1793 jan booysen will can be set aside rather than merely resisted, and the search has a new country to run in: the transvaal probate series, where this family turns out to have been living from at least the 1870s.

confirmed a second time, from an older source. the master of the supreme court's own index of death notices 1834–1912 has been read on film at the “beer, de” pages: the magdalena de beers in it are magda catha du plessis (1872), magda de beer (1865), magda vermeulen (1883), magda eliz troskie (1863), magda jacomina nel (1850) and magda greef (1839/40). no magdelena elisabeth, and nothing in 1843. so the absence is not an artefact of the modern naairs index. what is left is the published suid-afrikaanse geslagsregisters booysen genealogy, and dutch reformed baptism registers for graaff-reinet and paarl 1740–1790 read page by page rather than by index — his son was baptised at graaff-reinet in 1788. and now, newly available: the transvaal master’s series, where the same son died in 1876 — weeskamer records, rustenburg district registers, and the estates of the seven newly-named siblings. and on 13 september, from wikitree, the first hard pointer this question has ever had: its profile for petrus jacobus cites heese, suid-afrikaanse geslagsregisters, deel 1, page 331. this page has named that book as the route left since the beginning and marked it not yet followed, without a page number to follow it to. there is one now. the same profile also makes the father jan booysen rather than gerthardus lodewikus — against line 3 of the 1876 sterfkennis, which this archive has read — and that matters here because it is the same jan as the 1793 notarial will kab ncd 2/1: 49, the near-miss this question declined to adopt. a document outranks a tree and nothing has been changed. but the 1793 will is no longer a curiosity, and the disagreement now has a printed book and an exact page to be settled against. and an hour later, two more profiles settled it — in this archive's favour. jan booysen (boijens-9), baptised drakenstein 29 january 1741, married magdalena de beer on 21 january 1770 and married again on 15 december 1793. so his de beer wife was dead by december 1793; ours died in 1843, fifty years apart, which is exactly the objection this entry raised when it declined the 1793 will. the reasoning was right, and the will is now positively identified as his — a man remarrying in december 1793 is a man making a will that year. the tree's error is explained too: its own de beer profile (de_beer-638) carries the codes "b6c2 (and b6c6)", two baptisms nine years apart (1745 tulbagh, 1754 stellenbosch), and a sibling list holding both a magdalena and a magdalena elizabeth. two women merged into one profile is what put jan over our petrus jacobus. one gain: if ours is the second of the two, her parents are zaccharias de beer and anna pretorius — the first candidate this question has ever had for her side. a lead, needing the codes checked in print. and on 14 september the book was read, and it did not go this archive's way. de villiers 1893 is freely downloadable; page 34 marks only the 1754 magdalena “zie booijsen”, which is this archive's own birth year for her, so she is one woman and not two — the paragraph above is withdrawn and logged on /corrections/. page 78 then gives her husband as jan booijsen, baptised 29 january 1741, and their seventh child as “petrus jacobus, gedoopt 21 september 1788, gehuwd met anna maria van der merwe”, whose first child is “david schalk, gedoopt 4 januari 1807”. four fields agree with this archive and the fifth is the father. there is exactly one petrus jacobus of 21 september 1788 in the whole volume and exactly one david schalk of 4 january 1807, and the word lodewikus appears nowhere in it. and on 14 september a senior wikitree member offered a candidate for the name. riël smit: the only gerhardus booysen in de villiers & pama (1981) is b3c1d1 gerhardus loret booijsen, baptised september 1770 at drakenstein, and “maybe the loret changed to lodevicus over time”. this archive had already met that man in the 1893 text and not known what to do with him. he does not solve the question — he is b3c1d1, a son of booij and not of jan, which makes him petrus jacobus's first cousin rather than his father, and he was eighteen in 1788. but he is the first plausible source for the name on the 1876 notice, and the likeliest reading is now that the informant reached for a remembered family name and hung it on the wrong man. so this question has changed shape: it is no longer “who were gerthardus lodewikus's parents” but “did he exist?” he is in this archive on one line of one 1876 death notice, in the field that asks a family for the names of grandparents dead seventy years. nothing has been rewritten. but the notice is no longer the only evidence in the room, and the next step is the graaff-reinet baptism register for 21 september 1788, read directly. and on 15 september the last escape route closed and the mechanism was found. the standing objection was that pama’s 1981 revision might have moved him, in which case the death notice would stand unopposed. riël smit, who owns that edition: “yes, de villiers & pama (1981) still place petrus jacobus (b3c4d7) b. 21 sept 1788 under jan b3c4.” pieter van zyl searched for a marriage between a gerhardus lodewicus and a magdalena de beer and found none, noted that jan had been dead more than forty years when petrus jacobus died, and remembered from the notice itself that a child of petrus jacobus carried the name. he is right and the child is nine lines lower on the same sheet: line 12 lists eight children and the fifth is jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen. the name in the parents’ box is the back half of a son’s name in one clerk’s hand, and the half that was dropped is jan. the man who signed was hendrik stefanus, the seventh child, born about 1828, writing the name of a grandfather dead before he was ten. the spine has not been moved and that is deliberate: everything against gerthardus lodewikus is secondary — one printed genealogy agreeing with its own earlier edition is one source agreeing with itself — and what he has is a primary document signed by a son. jan booijsen is entered as inferred, not documented. and the screen route to the baptism is now known to be shut: the familysearch dutch reformed collection holds 54 registers for paarl (drakenstein), 48 for graaff-reinet and 55 for stellenbosch, and sorted earliest first the first row in every town is 1843. it is the post-1842 church archive series and it does not reach the eighteenth century at all.
what would settle it

the baptism entry of 21 september 1788 itself, at cape town. de villiers is not a source; he is an index to one, compiled from the doopregister. that entry names the father in a contemporary hand, written within days of the birth, by somebody with no reason to be confused. the originals are at the western cape archives, 72 roeland street; drakenstein first, since b3c4 jan was a burgher there, then graaff-reinet and stellenbosch. not reachable through familysearch — that collection begins in 1843.

the anglo-boer war museum's register of 12,792 cape rebels holds 26 booysens, every one from the northern cape or griqualand west. 'booyzen' returns nothing in any of the fifteen registers. the surname barry has now been searched, as this entry said it should be, and it returns four: barry, fred j., plaasboer of ivanhoe, district barkley-oos/wodehouse, tried june 1901 — the same district and the same month as daniel willem schoeman of caerlaverock, in whose house the family married five weeks later; barry, richard peter, plaasboer of jerpoint — and richard peter barry is kathleen barry's brother, the r. p. barry who signed his mother's 1915 death notice at manorowen, barkly east; plus adolf barry of keimoes and thomas andrew barry of oudtshoorn, neither relevant. identity is not proven — the register gives no birth dates or parents — but the claim that this family was rebel country now has two men of its own surname in its own district.

the anglo-boer war museum's fifteen registers contain no camp list at all, so this entry named the wrong source. the right one is the university of cape town's british concentration camps of the south african war 1900-1902 database, and it has now been searched. booyzen returns 5, and every one is transvaal — gert jacobus, aged 2, died johannesburg camp, farm rietvallei, district marico; gertruida magdalena, aged 19, died vereeniging camp, farm rietvlei, district heidelberg; jan gerhardus lodewicus, aged 2. none from the cape. and on 15 september the three were read on the database’s own pages, which do not say what this entry says. gert jacobus and gertruida magdalena are each recorded “died in camp: yes”, with farms — rietvallei, district marico, and rietvlei, district heidelberg — and gertruida carries the note “or irene rc”, so even her camp is uncertain. jan gerhardus lodewicus is recorded “died in camp: no”, with no camp and no farm at all. listing all three together as camp deaths was this archive’s compression, not the database’s. the source is named on every page: rs 25 transvaal death lists, national archives, pretoria — which is exactly why the caveat below is right, and the cause of death on all three is one word, ziekte. barry returns 0 in the entire database. booysen with catherine, kathleen, john barry, or willem hermanus all return 0, as does booyzen with catharina. so no member of this family has been found in a camp. important caveat: that database is built largely from camp death lists and surviving registers, so it records who died far better than who was interned and walked out. absence here is much weaker evidence than presence would have been, and this claim is not disproved — only unsupported.

cape camp registers proper rather than death lists — aliwal north is the camp nearest barkly east. also the cape colony refugee and 'undesirables' returns, which handled rebel families in the cape districts and are not in the uct database.
4 is the letter in the 1879 signature a z or an s? closed

answered, 13 september 2026, by a document twelve years older than the one this archive had been arguing from. the 1903 registration of his death — entry 74, district barkly east, made by his son richard barry, who was present when he died — enters question 5 as “irishman born in ireland”. it also gives his age as eighty-four years two months, his trade as carpenter, his residence and place of death as manor owen ward iv, his death as 25 august 1903, and the number of his children as eleven. the 1915 death notice that typed “at sea, exact whereabouts unknown, british” was sworn by a different son twelve years after the fact. where the two disagree this archive now follows 1903: it is closer to the man, its informant was in the room, and it is a statutory registration rather than an estate paper. the old text of this entry follows. partly answered. the 1915 death notice is now read: it types his birthplace as “at sea (exact whereabouts unknown), british” and his mother as “born neagle”. what remains is the other two documents, and the question of who his parents actually were.

checked against the settler roll for owen's party. every date the tree carried is right: gravesend 3 december 1819, the nautilus, table bay 17 march 1820, algoa bay 14 april 1820, fifty-two settlers. the roll adds an occupation nobody had — he is entered as a chemist, not the preacher or farmer this archive knew. and it adds ages: 'kolbe, george augustus 20. chemist. w margaret 19.' he was born 7 december 1802 and the ship sailed four days before his seventeenth birthday; she was born 23 february 1803. they were sixteen and sixteen. set beside the 1819 marriage allegation, where both swore they were twenty-one at sixteen and fifteen, that is two age overstatements in one year on two official documents. whether the second was theirs or the party organiser's cannot be told from the roll.

10 did the boys work on the mines? — yes. one did, and this archive had said there was none. medium

the last line of the testimony, now tested as far as it can be from here. no booyzen mining record appears anywhere in the national archives index, searched across all repositories for mine, miner and myn. that index covers government files rather than private company employment registers, so the absence is weak on its own — but it is not on its own. every occupation this archive has actually read for these men points somewhere else: willem hermanus is a boer in 1879 and a mason in 1905; george downing mountjoy is a boomkweker, a tree nurseryman, in 1924 and a clerk on the south african railways at his death in 1947; his grandfather was a farmer and his great-great-grandfather a saddler. not one miner among them. that sentence is now withdrawn. the indwe marriage register of 21 september 1908 enters william hermanus booyzen, aged 22, jonkman, under rang of beroep as mijnwerker, living at dugmore mijn — and his mother kathleen barry stood godmother at his son's font at indwe three months later, which is how this archive knows whose son he is. so the last line of the testimony is supported, and mislocated: indwe is a coal town in the north-eastern cape, this is 1908, and the testimony puts the mines after a train to johannesburg that had plainly not yet been taken. the negative was built on the occupations this archive happened to have read, and it had not read this one because it did not know the man existed.

private records rather than public ones: witwatersrand mining company employment registers, and johannesburg street directories 1905–1935 for booyzen at forest hill and mayfair. also the five transvaal estate files now identified, which will state each man's occupation at death. and now, first: dugmore colliery employment records if any survive, and the indwe registers read forward from 1910 for the rest of this man's life.
11 find the farm — and test the burning. and now a land register that is name-indexed, with booyzen in it. high

still untested, and two blind alleys closed now. he is a boer (farmer, of lady grey) at his marriage in 1879 and a mason at his death in 1905; something took the land away in between. the anglo-boer war museum's farm list was searched for caerlaverock, manorowen and wolwekloof and returned nothing — but that register turns out to be an orange free state land roll (farm number, morgen, square roods, owners), covering only winburg, fauresmith, vrede, rouxville, bethlehem, bloemfontein, hoopstad, kroonstad and philippolis. a control search on 'dordrecht' returns 670 cape rebels and 0 farms. the negative result is void, not informative.

13 september 2026: the cape series is identified. it is the war losses compensation commission, cape town archives repository, 1902 — the cape's equivalent of the transvaal cjc. kab returns 454 documents for compensation and war, and 679 for losses. booyzen returns 39 documents in kab overall and none of them in combination with losses or compensation; booysen returns 2,370 overall and exactly one in combination, a workmen's compensation act claim at king william's town in 1947. but the zero is weak and the control says so: smit, schoeman and barry also return nothing under losses, and the two botha hits turn out to be a 1935 locust and arsenical-poisoning stock claim from an entirely different series. the commission's files are catalogued by sub-commissioner and volume, not by claimant, so a name search cannot reach them. what is left is the commission's own claim registers, in the reading room at roeland street, which no search from here can substitute for. also still untouched: cape deeds and quitrent records for barkly east, lady grey and wodehouse, and cape district and refugee-camp records.
12 who were james montjoy's parents? — nobody at the cape knew, and now we know why: he arrived in uniform. high

read. kab mooc 6/9/21 ref 4393 was located by interpolating reference numbers across film 007844936 and found at image 339 of 2,223. (this archive published 338 and 338 is somebody else's family — corrected 9 october 2026 after both frames were opened: 338 is the death notice of christoffel hendrik olivier, trader, who died at his own house in the town of graaff-reinet on 15 june 1840, and 340 is willem jacobus van der merwe of bouwbosch fontein. the record ark 1:1:qp4z-wk68 opens at 339.) james montjoy, saddler, born in 'europe' about 1782, died at cradock in september 1827 leaving a house and erf worth £90 and four children under nine. line 3, names of the parents of the deceased: not known — written thirteen years after his death by a relative who knew his trade, his property and his wife's first husband. it also settles two things: our tree's 1827 death date is right (the 1840 file date is the filing year, and the contradiction was this archive's error), and anna catharina was indeed the widow of a pietersen, confirming the half-brother inference from the 1851 font.

nothing further inside south africa, and the 1817 marriage register now proves it rather than assuming it. that register has been found and read: he married anna catharina slier, widow of harmanus pieterzen, at graaff-reinet on 9 march 1817. cape entries of that date routinely record where a party came from, and three couples on that very page are entered 'beide van uitenhage' — but against james montjoy there is a ruled dash and nothing. the blank is not an artefact of the 1840 notice being written thirteen years after his death; it was already there at his wedding while he stood in the room. three documents have now been located that this archive had missed, because it filtered a search and wrote the filter up as the whole search: kab mooc 7/1/104: 42 — james mountjoy's will of 1818, joint with anna catharina slier, his wife, made a year after their marriage; kab mooc 7/1/104: 43 — the same pair again in 1827, the year he died; and kab co 3972: 17 — a colonial office memorial of 1834 from the widow of j mountjoy requesting remission of a fine, which is a petition in her own voice seven years after his death. a will of 1818 may state where the testator came from, and a memorial to the colonial office very often does. these are now the most likely documents in existence to break this wall, and none of them is digitised. as for the english end: findmypast returns 12,984 for the surname and birth year alone, and “a saddler in the cape by march 1817” will not narrow that — the way in is a cape arrival record, not an english birth record. and on 15 september the arrival record was named, by a man who slept in his house. john montgomery, founder of burgersdorp, in the friend of the free state of 25 november 1869, recalling his arrival at cradock in january 1822 when the village held about six people: “messrs. solomon and s.m. de beer, the rev. mr. evans, mr. p. gie, james mountjoy (a saddler, who was discharged from the 21st light dragoons), the two messrs. ziervogel, mr. heilberg, fieldcornet b.j. vorster, and gert van deventer. after some trouble i obtained lodgings for the night from mr. mountjoy.” there is no room in a village of six for two saddlers of one name. the 21st light dragoons were the cavalry of the cape garrison from the 1806 expedition. he did not arrive as a settler and no passenger list holds him, which is exactly why the 1817 marriage register rules a line through the column and leaves it blank and why his death notice says not known — the colony had no way to know. the army did. this entry is no longer blocked on a missing kind of document; it is waiting on a named one, in a building in london.

wo 97 at the national archives, kew — royal hospital chelsea soldiers’ documents, arranged by regiment for discharges before 1855, giving a man’s parish and county of birth, his age at enlistment, his trade and his service. with it wo 12, the muster books and pay lists, which show when he stopped appearing and where the regiment was. neither is digitised for this regiment. the three cape documents named above — the 1818 and 1827 wills and the 1834 colonial office memorial — are still worth having and are still not digitised, but they are no longer the only route, and they were never the likeliest one.

answered. the sign-in came back on 16 september and the question fell in under an hour — not to a name search, which this entry correctly said was closed, but to the relationship search: father john barry, mother a kolbe, child's own name left blank. nine baptisms come back for the couple, and two of them were not in this archive. margrith louisa maria, baptised at burgersdorp on 5 april 1852 — indexed twice, as “margrith louisa maria” and “margreth louisa mary”, and with no surname of her own either time, which is the blank name column that hid her sister of 1855. and william frederick thomas barry, born 29 september 1861 and baptised at graaff-reinet — invisible for the opposite reason, because he carries the same name as the brother baptised in 1853 and a name search returns that one and stops. nine baptisms plus hendrik nicholaas and richard peter makes eleven, which is exactly what the 1903 registration says. margaret mary of the death notices is almost certainly margrith louisa maria — it is her mother's name and there is no other candidate. and two williams eight years apart means the first died. this entry's own reasoning was right and its conclusion was too narrow: an index that cannot produce four children known to exist will not produce two unknown ones by name. it produced them both by relationship. the old text follows. the baptism register behind the 1868 entry, which needs the record identifier familysearch refused on 13 september with http 403. read it and it either names john augustus barry and margaretha kolbe or it does not, and either way the question moves. the second missing child has no candidate at all; the same relationship search, run on the father instead of the mother, has not been tried.
15 who were the commandant's twelve children? — one named from a document, and two candidates since high

the obituary of john gerson eliezar kolbe, dead at leeuwberg on 3 april 1868, says he left “a widow and 12 children”, and the friend's version — which the grahamstown reprint drops — counts them: “of the eight sons and four daughters he has left behind him”. only one daughter was married and the youngest child was an infant; two sons had been serving with him in the field. not one of the twelve was named in it. exactly one has since been reached from a document: the free state criminal court of 1869, reporting a horse theft at springfield, ward upper modder-river, in october 1868, lists among the stolen animals “1 blue schimmel mare, with foal, the property of john kolbe, jun.” — beside a black mare belonging to “anna jacoba van der merwe, widow of late j.g.e. kolbe”. a son, holding stock in his own right beside his mother six months after the death. a search engine offers thirty-one more, born between 1843 and 1869, which is exactly the window between the marriage and the death — and every one of the thirty-one is tree data, other people's trees indexed. thirty-one plausible children do not become evidence by being plausible together, and none has been entered. 21 september 2026 — two more candidates, and neither is proof. south africa, civil marriage records, 1801–1974 holds anna jacoba kolbe × francis mccabe, 13 july 1871, and jan hendrik kolbe × rose maria mccabe, bloemfontein, 4 june 1872 — two of the landdrost's daughters marrying two kolbes in ten months, in the town the commandant's whole public life was attached to, four years after he died and while his widow was married to that same landdrost. jan hendrik is given as 23, born about 1849, which sits correctly among children of a man who married in 1843. but the index carries the couple and no parents. it was read through this archive's own image-data route and the record holds nothing else, so the fathers are on the image and the image has not been read. until somebody reads that handwriting, these two are kolbes of the right name in the right town at the right moment and the link to him is borrowed from a user tree. one named from a document; two waiting on one. vab mhg m777, his widow's 1896 estate, would name all twelve outright.

three documents, none of them online. vab mhg k71, his own estate, and vab mhg m777, his widow's — she died in 1896 under the name of her second husband, which is why she was hard to find. and now a third and possibly better one: the estate of francis mccabe, landdrost of bloemfontein, who married her about april 1871 and died on 23 february 1872 leaving “four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children”. an executor listing step-children by name would answer this from the opposite side. also: the friend and the grahamstown journal read forward from 1868 for their marriages and deaths — the method that has already produced john kolbe junior, a grandson killed by lightning in 1884, and a gersom eliezär kolbe born in the year his father died.
14 does elizabetha van der merwe exist anywhere but her son's death notice? — three routes closed. medium

nothing at that state.

held as data since 17 september 2026. it was written inline before that, as a list of tuples destructured into five names — and two of the sixteen carry a sixth field, what has been tried, which the destructure never reached. those two are §0, this archive's oldest wall, and §12, james montjoy's parents: the page printed their whole what-would-settle-it paragraph where the priority label goes, and showed what had been tried under the heading where to look. the fields are named now, so a row can gain one without silently shifting the rest.

the state of a question is set by hand, one at a time, and never read off its own heading. seven headings here announced an answer while the row still carried a priority. deriving the state from the words would have marked all seven shut, and two of the seven are not. §3 — were the women and children in a camp — reports a negative result from one database and names two unread sources that would settle it, the cape camp registers proper and the cape refugee and undesirables returns. §10 — did the boys work on the mines — corrects a claim this archive had made rather than closing the question, and still points at mining company registers, street directories, five transvaal estate files and the indwe registers. both stay open at the priority they had. the five that are shut were shut by a document: §5 by the 1903 death registration entering irishman born in ireland, §6 by yorkshire burials returning zero barrys at bilsdale in an indexed run, §8 by there being nothing left on those profiles, §9 by the settler roll, §13 by a relationship search naming both missing children. answered means a document answered the question as asked; closed, which only §4 carries, means the question itself went away.
archives identified and not yet worked

naairs — the national automated archival information retrieval system, south africa. the single most important unopened door: it indexes cape (kab) and transvaal (tab) estate files and death notices, which is where a death notice for willem hermanus booyzen would be found.

cape archives (kab), master's office (mooc) — one reference is already in hand: mooc 6/9/35: 7698 (1845), the estate of george augustus kolbe. that one has since been read — it is published in full, and on 20 september it caught an error in a historian’s draft that cites it as his own first source. the notice → the rest of the master's office holdings are still unopened.

the dutch reformed church registers for graaff-reinet, cradock, colesberg, burgersdorp, dordrecht and barkly east — already the backbone of the tree's citations, but read only where familysearch has indexed them.

anglo-boer war records — camp registers, cape rebel registers, special tribunal files, the list of the 44 executed for high treason, and the national scouts rolls that would test the "joiners" half of the story.

findmypast and familysearch — both hold transcripts already cited in the tree (one findmypast transcript reference, r_177176049779, is recorded against the 1812 birth) and neither has been systematically searched for this surname.

§ 16 · high priority
who are the mountjoys of barkly oost? — answered

found by accident, on the page opposite a booyzen baptism: the doop register, barkly oost, 6 october 1889 records hercules johannes mountjoy and maria sophia van niekerk baptising a son, with jakobus jonathan mountjoy and maria sophia mountjoy among the witnesses.

this line descends from johanna catharina mountjoy (1819–1863), of whom the archive has little more than a surname and a father who died in 1827. here are three named mountjoys in the right district, twenty-six years after her death.

answered they are the descendants of johanna catharina mountjoy's brother. george mountjoy (b. 1823, cradock), saddle maker, married maria sophia botha at cradock in 1848 and had thirteen children. hercules johannes (the father at the 1889 font) and james/jakobus jonathan (the witness, who died at barkly east in 1937) are two of his sons. the child baptised that day, george mountjoy (1889–1963), was a second cousin of the booyzen daughter baptised in the same register three weeks earlier. the branch →

now confirmed from originals the parentage no longer rests on a user-edited tree. the dutch reformed baptism register records herculas johannes mountjoy, born 16 july 1866, baptised 29 july 1866, father george mountjoy, mother maria sophia botha. his 1941 death registration gives his age as 74 — a man born in july 1866 is 74 in may 1941. his marriage at dordrecht on 8 october 1888, aged 22, is a year before the 1889 font. the chain closes.

james jonathan is "james john." his estate is kab mooc 6/9/5047, ref 58379 (1938), and his wife's is the very next file, 58380 — maria louisa bertha née kumm. their children's baptisms enter the father under both name forms and spell the mother's surname five ways (kumm, kuen, kunn, kum, keem).

hercules johannes has no estate file at all. the cape town archives were searched under mountjoy (42 documents; all 22 dated 1930 or later read in full), montjoy (4), and mountjoy combined with herklaas, hercules, wodehouse and barkly (0 each). the estates around him run 1938, 1939, 1943, 1946, 1948 — an unbroken sequence, so this is an absence rather than a gap in the index. the likeliest reading is an estate too small to report.

tested again, and it holds the cape probate collection has now been read for every indexed mountjoy at once — 61 personas, the whole surname in the whole collection. hercules johannes returns exactly one hit, and it is his mother-in-law's. his name is written on her 1902 death notice, in the list of her children, and the index keys every name on a page. the absence is real, and this is what it looks like from the inside. her notice →

what is left: the four small corrections for our own tree — sleer/slier vs schleher (the 1863 death notice now settles this in favour of an l), the 1817 graaff-reinet marriage, thomas jacobus living to 1827, and the missing sibling jacoba catharina (1820–1842).
§ 15 · high priority
why was kathleen barry a "military pensioner"?

her 1940 death certificate records her, at eighty-two, as a military pensioner. her husband had been dead thirty-five years and died of a stomach ulcer. 13 september 2026 — one candidate found and rejected the same day. a ninth son turned up in the brixton burial register, richard peter booyzen, dead at twenty-four on 25 october 1918, in the middle of an epidemic that killed thousands of south african servicemen and pensioned their dependants. his death registration says he was a married sawyer of 18 anderson street, turffontein, dead of influenza and pneumonia after eleven days. not a soldier. the question stands, and is now sharper for it: the pension belongs to a son who served and survived. this archive guessed a son killed in the first world war, with a dependant's pension.

searched — and the guess is wrong. the south africa war graves project holds no booyzen among the first world war dead (its two booyzens died in 1944 and 1993), and of thirteen booysen deaths in 1914–18, not one matches a son by forename — and most are in the native labour corps, cape coloured labour regiment and military labour bureau, units not open to a family recorded as "european" on every certificate this archive has read. decisively: all her identifiable sons survived — dying in 1932, 1952, 1956, 1966 and 1980.
so the pension belongs to a man who served and came home — a disabled son with his mother as dependant, or another entitlement altogether.

where to look now: the sandf documentation centre, pretoria (personnel archives and reserves, 20 visagie street), which holds union defence force attestation papers, personnel files and pension files from 1912. none of it is online, and it needs a written request. note also that the cwgc site is behind a bot check and was not searched, and that familysearch's south african defence collection is browse-by-image and not name-indexed.

request sent, 9 sept 2026 a letter has gone to the documentation centre at both published addresses, asking three things: whether a pension file exists in her name; on whose service it rested; and whether any of her eight named sons appears in udf attestation or personnel records for 1914–18 or 1939–45, and whether an attestation names his mother as next of kin. see requests/sandf-documentation-centre-pension.md.

the strength of the request is that it runs the search backwards. we have no service number for any son — but we know there was a pension, and we know the pensioner's name, her exact address and her date of death. the pension registers can be searched on those.
§ 14 · high priority
did any of the bond street money reach the cape?

johan gottlieb kolbe's 1842 will divides his residue among his children, with the issue of any dead child taking that child's share, and a later clause names "my said children or grandchildren" outright. george augustus kolbe died eleven months before his father. on paper his share therefore fell to his children at burgersdorp — including margaretha kolbe, who married john augustus barry.

where to look: the pcc estate and accounting papers behind the 1846 probate (tna, prob series); the cape estate files for margaret downing (estate 4094, 1868) and for the barry marriage settlement; and any correspondence between timothy duke of lombard street and the cape.
§ 13 · medium priority
test the deeper kolbe and downing pedigrees

the tree carries kolbe back to 1699 in württemberg and downing back to 1683, through the surnames jung, larman, trick, heard, hooper and king. none of it has been tested, and margaret downing's own death notice names neither of her parents.
where to look: london parish registers for st anne's soho and st leonard's shoreditch; devon parish registers for trick, heard and hooper; württemberg lutheran church books for kolbe and jung.

the last version of this page said one document would change more than any amount of further reasoning — the death record of willem hermanus booyzen. it was found, and it did. it gave a date (13 september 1905), a place (doorn street, indwe), a cause (ulcer of the stomach, fourteen months), an occupation (mason), an informant (his eldest son), and — four lines apart on one page — both spellings of the surname. the documents →
it had been sitting in the family tree's own photo store, unread, the whole time. that is the lesson worth keeping: look at what you already have before you go looking for more.

/errands/.title: Errands — The Booyzen Archive
blocks: 7 doors · 57 things that could be settled behind them · 23 letters, 10 still owed an answer

four questions in this archive now end at a building rather than a search box. this page is what somebody standing at each door could settle, with the references written out so nobody has to find them twice.
why this page exists

four separate questions in this archive now end at a door rather than a screen. this page is what somebody standing at each of those doors could settle, with the references written out so they do not have to be looked up again.

everything on this site was read from australia, off microfilm, through a browser. that has taken the work a long way and it has now stopped in four specific places — not for want of searching, but because the records are restricted, unfilmed, or catalogued in a way no name search can reach.

thirteen letters have gone out and three have been answered; ten more are drafted and unsent. the letters, and what came back ↓ if you are near any of these buildings, or know somebody who is, the references below are complete and every one has been checked against a catalogue or a film. sources →
national archives repository, pretoria
private bag x236, pretoria 0001 · (+27) 12 441 3207 · enquiries2@dsac.gov.za

national archives repository, pretoria — estate files whose familysearch films refuse to serve images — film 007830063 and every film after it returns 403, and those are exactly the ones running to 1946 and later. a letter went on 13 september 2026 and has not been answered; a private researcher was engaged on the 16th and stood down on the 20th. this list has been cut by more than half, on purpose. every death notice on it was tested first against the familysearch family tree, geni and the myheritage capture, and three came out answerable for nothing. what is left is either something no tree holds, or something a tree asserts that only a document can prove — and each item below says which.
each was tested against the free trees first. these are the ones that came back empty, or came back contradicted.
— the three death notices that survived the check —

the biggest single question available at this depot, and a single page. surviving spouse hester gertina susanna born joubert. “downing” is carried here as a forename — it was the maiden name of margaret downing, who married the 1820 settler at shoreditch in 1819 — and if this notice names his father it may tie the transvaal kolbes to the settler directly, which everything in this archive reaches by inference and nothing else. why it survived the check: he was not found on the familysearch tree — but that tree's search is scored, not filtered (narrow queries return 27,656 and 110,097 rows), so a nil return there means nothing at all. untested rather than answered.
tab mhg 40293 — kolbe, frederick fortunatus downing, 1918

from the second marriage — the thinnest branch in this archive. married isabella frederika coetsee at middelburg in 1896. why it survived: familysearch g5dk-wzs has him, with the right birth — 19 january 1870, middelburg — and gives parents only. no death, no wife, no children. the tree is silent on everything this notice would give.
tab mhg 5155/51 — gert jacobus booyzen, b. 19 jan 1870

railway clerk, forest hill. his wife's file, mhg 2945/44, is read. in the direct line. why it survived, and it is not the reason originally given: his children are already known. but the myheritage capture gives his death as 21 february 1947 where this archive has 11 december 1947 off the johannesburg burial register, with burial on the 14th. one of the two is wrong and only his own death notice settles which. a document proving what a tree asserts wrongly.
tab mhg 1095/48 — george downing mountjoy booyzen, 1947
court papers, school correspondence, war-compensation claims and state files. no family tree holds any of these, so they were never candidates for the check and they stand as they were.
— the items no tree could ever answer —

found 16 september and not yet on any list. the marriage transcriptions hold “1895 · jan gerhardus sodeunicus booyzen × antonetta petronella magdalena snyman” — the same couple, married 1895, divorced 1903. this archive holds a jan gerhardus lodewicus booysen born 4 december 1855 of whom it has said for months that nothing is known of what became of him, and a jgl booyzen signing the money papers of a farm school at kwaggafontein in 1898–99. three sightings in one decade and no proof they are one man. wanted: the summons and any order — a divorce summons gives the date and place of marriage, the residence, and usually the children. reference confirmed on naairs: depot tab, source wld, volume_no 0, reference 302/1903.
tab wld 302/1903 — illiquid case. divorce. jan gerhardus lodewicus booysen vs antonetta petronella magdalena (born snyman)

the seven marico compensation claims, 1903–04. read on the index today and they give nothing but initials: jpj, pj, gl, jpj, l, jc, he booyzen. no forename, no farm, no amount, no remarks. the index line is the whole record and no screen anywhere will improve it. seven thin files in one building. what is wanted from each is the claimant's full name, his farm and his field-cornetcy — enough to say whether any of the seven is this family. gl is the one to open first.

forty-eight documents of one farm school in marico, eight of them signed by a jgl booyzen. what is wanted is his signature and his full name — the head of a letter gives initials, the foot of one gives a name. or262/98 (the subsidy application), or6919/98 (the £61-6-0 deficit) and or7499/99 (the £8 argument) are the three most likely to carry it. if he signs jan gerhardus lodewicus, the man born 4 december 1855 stops being a blank.
tab od — the kwaggafontein school file, 1897–1900, and or13059/97 with it

the school on this family's own farm. its money papers are signed ds. booysen and ds booijsen. one question only: is ds. a pair of initials — david schalk — or the dutch ds., for dominee? one glance at a signature answers it. or2037/99 is the letter about school materials for orphans and is the one worth copying whatever the answer.
tab od or19199/98, or19484/98 and or2037/99 — vaalbank, district lichtenburg

a different source, same building — sab, not tab. a farm owner at barkly east and his son, both r.p.k. barry, with a state file between them. this archive holds one richard pieter kolbe barry born 1899 and cannot say which of the two he is. wanted: whatever states ages or relationship — one page will do. vwr is the department of social welfare.
sab vwr 2, b645/8/38, 1937 — “aansoek deur plaaseienaar. barkly-oos. rpk barry. bywoner rpk barry (seun).”

david schalk booijzen (born cradock, 9 june 1848) — alive and fifty-six at goedehoop, pretoria on 27 november 1905 and lost to this archive from that day. no estate file and no civil death can be found for him, and none for his second wife johanna elena born stols, widow lowies, either. if the master's own estate index at pretoria carries either of them, that is the answer. their two known estate numbers are 4795 (his first wife, 1900) and 7081 (her first husband, 1905), so the pair were certainly known to that office.
an index search, not a file — david schalk booijzen

jacobus nichols booyzen, 1923. corrected 22 september: this archive had it as a doubtful reference and it is not. anne brest found it on naairs on 15 september, sent the link, and explained the thing that had been read as a fault: the year suffix is simply absent on some references of that period. this archive could not find it on microfilm and is not name-indexed under any booyzen spelling — both true, and neither meant the reference was wrong. wanted: the file, and the death notice in it. he is the eldest of the eight on the 1863 death notice and the only “major” on that list.
tab mhg 52653 — a file, located by the researcher on naairs
three were on this list on 15 september and are not now. each was answered without the archive, and each is recorded so the work is not repeated.
— dropped, and why, so nobody orders them again —

wanted for her parents, and called on 15 september “the most wanted page in this list”. her parents were already here: baptised at barkly oost, 24 may 1891, entry 120, and her brother henry james at barkly east in 1887 with the register naming willem hermanus booÿsen and catharina maria sophia barry outright. the stated reason had been answered for a fortnight and the row still carried it.
dropped · tab mhg 3734/46 — catherine mary sophia daschner

wanted for his children, because his brakpan gravestone says “aan ons vader” and this archive could not name one of them. familysearch m87r-4x4 names ten, with a wife — margritha maria susanna poole, 1886–1947 — and a birth and death (26 april 1884; 23 january 1952 at delmas) that match the gravestone to the day. the two eldest are willem hermanus and catharina maria sophia, his own parents’ names, which is this family’s documented naming pattern and is the check that the profile is really him. a tree, so not proof — but paying for ten names that can be read for nothing is buying the wrong thing.
dropped · tab mhg 769/52 — john barry booyzen

already the most documented man of his generation here: baptism (barkly east, 12 august 1887, register naming both parents), marriage, death, burial, and a cause of death corrected twice off a pension form. a death notice would repeat what five documents already say.
dropped · tab mhg 10/57 — henry james booyzen

wanted to “confirm he is a son of catherine mary sophia daschner”. he already is: he sits among the eleven children, and two independent sources agree on him — the eggsa stone (“daschner willie 1915–1963 & millie harding 1926–2004”, west park) and the naairs estate index. what remains is his own children, and he is a collateral. lowest value on the list; dropped.
dropped · tab mhg 2703/63 — daschner, william herman

flagged as probably wrong. this archive has carried “tab mhg o/2899, jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen, d. 25 may 1885, vaalbank, district lichtenburg” for days, and on 16 september it would not reproduce on naairs under booijsen, booysen or booijzen paired with gerhardus, lodewicus or lodewikus. the estate may exist under a spelling not yet tried, or the reference may be a rendering rather than a call number. it is not worth an hour of anybody's morning until this archive can produce it from the index itself.
tab mhg o/2899 — do not hunt for this one

20 september 2026 — a visit was booked and then stood down, and this list is why. a private researcher, anne brest, was engaged on 16 september and was to go on tuesday the 22nd. she was asked not to, two days out, and invoice 463 was set aside. the reason given to her was the true one: the list had been changed four times in five days, and on checking it properly two of the six files turned out to be answerable from sources this archive already had. she would have spent the day photographing at least one file nobody needed. what was promised in exchange was one list, every item checked first. this is it. the rule it was built on: a tree gives you names to look for; a death notice gives you proof. both are worth having, but they are not worth the same money, and an item survives here only if it says which of the two it is buying. and the test has a trap in it: familysearch's tree search is scored, not filtered — narrow queries return tens of thousands of rows — so “not found there” is never evidence of anything. two items survive on exactly that basis and say so. — — — 15 september 2026: ms mavis xaba, archivist assistant in the reading room, replied to the letter of 12 september: “all the estate files you are requesting are bound files. unfortunately, we are therefore unable to scan these files and provide complete digital copies by email.” she did not say any reference was wrong — including mhg 52653. she named the private researcher.
pietermaritzburg archives repository

231 pietermaritz street · private bag x9012, pietermaritzburg 3200 · 033 342 4712 · fax 033 394 4353 · the provincial archivist — and the email is in doubt: the national archives' own page gives pmbarchives@dact.kzntl.gov.za on a record last touched in 2015, and kzntl.gov.za is a retired provincial domain; current listings give pmbarchives@kzndac.gov.za. post it, or telephone first and ask.

pietermaritzburg archives repository — six natal estate files, and until today this archive had two. familysearch's filmed natal probate series stops at 1950 and every one of these is later, so there is no screen that will ever show them. the address is now checked against the repository's own entry. a letter is drafted and not sent — requests/pietermaritzburg-archives-natal-estates.md. four of the six were found on 14 september, two of them by learning who two women already in this archive's search log actually were.
kolbe, frederik fortunatus hofmeyr, born naauwpoort, wakkerstroom. the settler's son's name in a fourth generation.
kolbe, hendrik johannes hofmeyr, born wakkerstroom.
beukes, petronella jacoba adriana, born kolbe, born in colesberg — now known to be the seventh of frederik fortunatus kolbe's eight children, baptised at colesberg 18 november 1877.

oosthuizen, pierre francois, born colesberg, spouse adriana henrietta johanna, born kolbe — the youngest of the eight, baptised at bethulie 23 october 1881. her husband's file, not hers, so the page wanted is the one naming spouse and children.

barry, henry james kolbe, born in barkly east, unmarried. a barry forename and a kolbe surname in one man — and dying unmarried, his file should name parents or siblings rather than a widow. the most wanted page in this list.
mountjoy, christian, born in barkly east, surviving spouse a mountjoy.

found 15 september, after the letter was drafted. a second barkly east mountjoy who died in natal, alongside christian mountjoy already on this list. barkly east is the town this family farmed in from about 1859, and two people leaving it for natal is a pattern rather than an accident. her death notice should name her parents.
nab msce 581/1973 — shooter, mathilda elizabeth, born mountjoy, born in barkly east

the wife of a man already on this list. msce 965/1956 is his; this is hers, twenty-two years earlier, and it gives him a wife's name and maiden surname this archive did not have. if only one of the two can be copied, hers is earlier and more likely to name his parents.
nab msce 21335/1934 — kolbe, johanna maria, born potgieter, spouse hendrik johannes hofmeyr kolbe

the couple this archive derived from baptism registers, confirmed from the other end. frederik fortunatus kolbe, born bethulie 1839, the settler's tenth child, married elizabeth johanna du toit — and both their estates are in natal. his file is cross-referenced to hers in the index. wanted: his death notice, which should name his parents and settle whether the natal kolbes descend from the settler.
nab msce 8509/1923 and 15161/1929 — elizabeth johanna kolbe, born du toit, and frederick fortunatus kolbe

a seventh is worth adding if anyone is already in the building: nab msce 4064/1974, booyzen, nicolaas theodorus, born in wakkerstroom. this archive expects that to be a coincidence of surname and town and would like to be told so.
free state archives repository, bloemfontein
vab — the depot this archive had never opened until 15 september 2026

free state archives repository, bloemfontein — commandant john gerson eliezar kolbe died in the orange free state in 1868 leaving twelve children, and this archive cannot name one of them. two files in bloemfontein would answer it. neither is filmed and neither is name-indexed beyond the line quoted here.

a memoir by a man of this family, and the only one known to exist. cited by fransjohan pretorius, military history journal vol. 8 no. 3, at page 78 — so it is a document of some length, not a note. if it is willem johannes kolbe (1847–1941), the settler's grandson who led the bloemfontein commando, it is a grandson of the settler describing his own life in his own words, and it may name his brothers and sisters — which is the twelve-children question. wanted: page 78, the extent of the item, and any recorded author or date. the identification rests on initials and is not proved: a renier-versameling at pretoria lists correspondence with a “p kolbe”, so the collection is split across depots and the collector dealt with more than one kolbe. the journal prints “al 19”; read as a1 19.
vab a1 19, renier-versameling, no. 244 — herinneringe van genl. w j kolbe, p. 78

kolbe, john gerson eleazar. eggenote anna jacoba (gebore van der merwe), 1868. the settler's eldest son — commandant of the district, j.p., director of the bloemfontein bank. the death notice should list the twelve children.

mccabe, anna jacoba, nooiensvan van der merwe, eggenote john gherson [kolbe], 1896. his widow, under her second husband's name, twenty-eight years on. her notice should name the same children as adults — which is better, because it would give their married surnames. 20 september — and it now has something to be checked against. two collaborative trees name the commandant’s children and give anna jacoba van der merwe as 1824–1896, which matches this estate’s year exactly. trees are not evidence and none of the twelve is adopted here — but ordering a document you can check beats ordering one you cannot.

his own words, if they were minuted. the commandant's obituary says that on his deathbed he told the doctor and the others present that this state had taken too much land from the basutos, that he had always thought so and had said so in the raad, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the governor for an equitable boundary. if the may 1867 session minuted him, that is a man's political position in his own voice, a year before he died of a war he thought unjust. the printed notulen are held here and are not online — hathitrust has some years and is behind bot protection, and this archive will not go around that.
the volksraad minutes for may 1867 — notulen der verrigtingen van den hoogedelen volksraad

the other way into the twelve. he married the commandant's widow about april 1871 and died fifteen months later leaving “a widow, four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children”. those step-children are the twelve. an executor listing them by name would answer from the opposite side to vab mhg m777, which is not readable online. naairs was down when this was raised and the reference has not been looked up.
vab estate of francis mccabe, landdrost of bloemfontein, d. 23 february 1872

c129 names both wives — maria petronella elisabetha antoinetta raath and anna gebore van der merwe. wanted: the heirs, and any list of children or step-children, which is the whole point. do not travel for bc11: the index says outright “bevat geen sterfkennis nie”, it contains no death notice, and the depot has saved somebody a wasted morning by writing it down. 20 september — this one is now worth more than it was. c129 names mccabe’s first wife as maria petronella elisabetha antoinetta raath. this archive separately holds a bloemfontein baptism of 1890 naming a mother maria petronella elizabeth antoinetta mccabe — the same four-part name, carrying mccabe as a surname. she is almost certainly his daughter by raath, named for her mother entire, and she married a frederik fortunatus kolbe. if the kolbe she married is the commandant’s son, a stepbrother married a stepsister nine years after their parents’ eleven-month marriage. what is wanted from c129 is precisely the list of daughters, which would prove it.
vab mhg c129 — francis mccabe, 1872, and vab 1/3/1/12 bc11, his insolvent estate

leonora steenkamp born kolbe · margaret downing fick born kolbe · georgina augusta de wet born kolbe · jacobus wynand louw kolbe · george augustus kolbe · catharina elizabeth malan born kolbe. six people of one surname applying together is a sibling group, and applications like this are usually about a parent's estate — so the file should name the parent. the first free state kolbe sibling group this archive can name at all. 15 september — the parents are now named, on an inference the file would settle. vab mhg k1431 gives “kolbe, george augustus, eggenote hester jacoba jacomina (gebore louw)”, 1905, and vab mhg 1/2/1/1 ks3 puts her estate under curatorship that same year — which is what happens when there are minor children. one of the six applicants is jacobus wynand louw kolbe, carrying his mother's maiden name, and another is george augustus kolbe, carrying his father's. if the 1931 file names a parent, it should name one of those two — and k1431 and 27114 are then the two estates to read next.
vab hg 4/2/1/1/456, 702/1931 — six kolbes applying to the court together

also worth an hour while anyone is in the building: the free state volksraadsnotule for may 1867, the “corn peace”, in which he spoke against the boundary — and the farms leeuwberg, where he died, and kaalspruit, where he settled about 1850 and lies. 21 september — the first three of these are now in one letter, requests/free-state-archives-kolbe-three.md: the memoir, m777 and k71. the rest of this list is deliberately held back, and the letter asks the repository whether they would rather have them in the same order or separately.
western cape archives, 72 roeland street, cape town
021 483 4000 · reading room mon–fri 08:00–16:00 · archives.clientservices@westerncape.gov.za

western cape archives, 72 roeland street, cape town — two documents that would break the oldest wall in this archive, and one series that cannot be searched by name from anywhere. a letter went on 9 september 2026 and has not been answered.

the oldest document this family has, and the one it owes most. the index line names eleven enslaved people of the household — silvia, lena, sara, janna, dorinda, fortuijn, meij and februarij van de caab; dijk and farla van madagascar; achilles van mallabaar. wanted entire: every name and valuation on the list, and the heirs, because if the heirs include a jan then this archive's direct line runs straight through this document. the tanap transcription project put these inventories online and its database no longer resolves, so there is no screen route left. also wanted: mooc 8/56.16a and 16b (zacharias booijsen, graaff reinet, 1805 and 1806), mooc 8/42.46 (aletta booyzen, graaff reinet, 1820), mooc 8/46.59 (jan lowies booijsen, onder roggeveld, 1831) and mooc 8/48.32 (piet booijsens, 1832).
mooc 8/18.11 — the inventory of gerrit booijsen, 13 december 1781, drakenstein

answered 18 september 2026 and off this list. melanie geustyn, senior librarian at the national library of south africa, sent all four pages three days after the enquiry went in, together with a two-page draft dsab entry by karel schoeman that was in the background file. the question this errand was written to answer — whether the letter carries a london address — is answered no: the heading is “london” and nothing finer, so brunswick square against conduit street is still open. nobody needs to stand at this door for it. left here, answered, rather than deleted, because an errand that quietly vanishes teaches nothing.
answered · sa library, cape town — msb751, the ga kolbe collection

the index has now been read; the originals have not. on 19 september the familysearch index for indwe and barkly east was worked past 1910, and the useful discovery was about which book is which: indwe is a lidmate roll — a membership register, not a baptism register — which is where a colliery town's incomers are written down and is a different book from the one this archive had assumed. it gave johanna catharina mountjoy joining on 23 july 1907, seven weeks after willem hermanus booijzen was confirmed in the same congregation on 31 may 1907. two families this archive follows, in one small coal town, in one winter. it does not make them relatives; it makes them neighbours, which is a fact and was not one before. what the originals would still settle: what became of willem hermanus booyzen after 1907, which the index does not say.

bessborough road, richmond tw9 4du, united kingdom · nationalarchives.gov.uk · reading rooms tue–sat, free, ticket required

the national archives, kew — british army records — this is a new country for this archive and it is here because of one sentence in a newspaper. john montgomery, who lodged in his house at cradock in january 1822, describes james mountjoy as “a saddler, who was discharged from the 21st light dragoons”. james montjoy's own death notice answers the question “names of the parents of the deceased” with not known, and his 1817 marriage register rules a line through the column that should say where he came from. nobody at the cape knew, because he did not arrive as a settler — he arrived in uniform. the army knew.

the discharge paper. arranged by regiment for discharges before 1855. it gives the man's parish and county of birth, his age at enlistment, his trade before enlisting, his service and the reason for discharge. a saddler born about 1782 and a civilian at the cape by 1817 — he married at graaff-reinet on 9 march 1817 — should be discharged in the years either side of that. one page ends a question this site has carried as blocking since it was written. note the index trap: on findmypast the same regiment sits under four different index strings holding different record series — “21st dragoons” returned 342 records with no wo 97 among them, while “21st regt of light dragoons” returned 128 that were nothing else. a negative against one spelling is worthless, and the same is likely true of kew’s own catalogue.
wo 97 — royal hospital chelsea, soldiers' documents, 21st light dragoons

the piece is now named, and the window is four quarters wide. this errand used to say “wo 12” and mean the whole series. two things narrowed it. first, the regiment left the cape for india in september 1817, not 1816 — printed in five london papers, the sun, the star, the public ledger and two others — and this archive had carried 1816 with no source behind it. so a man discharged at the cape leaves the musters in 1816–17, and wo 12/1450 alone should contain the quarter he disappears from. second, discovery spells the regiment “21st dragoons (light)” and will not find it spelled any other way. a muster also carries the trooper’s name in the paymaster’s hand and the place of each quarterly muster, which is how a man who stayed behind is told from a man who sailed.
wo 12/1450 — muster books and pay lists, 21st dragoons (light)

men discharged at the cape rather than shipped home are the ones who stayed and married into the colony. if there is a list of them, james mountjoy should be on it — and so, probably, should several other names this archive has met without explanation.
anything on the regiment's disbandment at the cape

/worklist/.title: The work list — The Booyzen Archive
blocks: 220 items, 63 of them open
what is being done here, as opposed to what is known.
why this page exists

every other register on this site answers what this archive knows. /searched/ holds every query ever run, /open-questions/ holds what is not known, /errands/ holds what can only be got through a door, and /corrections/ holds what was got wrong. none of them answers what is being done — and so for weeks that lived in a chat window, which is the one place that does not survive the session. this page is that list. it is deliberately not a list of findings. it is who is doing what, who is waiting on whom, and what was decided against and why.

the other registers on this site are about the family. this one is about the work, which means it is the only page here that is mostly about this archive's own limits — what it is waiting on, what it cannot reach, and what it set out to do and had to strike because the plan rested on something untrue.

an item here with no owner would be wallpaper, so the build refuses one, and an item open for six weeks is marked as such rather than left to look like something raised this morning. from item 24 this becomes a roadmap rather than a diary. those items were not raised by anything going wrong; they are the work this archive can see from where it now stands, in four groups and in the order it intends to take them. ten depot campaigns that have never been run — whole indexes this archive has taken single files out of without ever sweeping. seven checks, all of them owned by a machine, because every convention that has held here held when a build refused and every one that drifted was written down and watched by nobody. six pieces of publishing debt, which is what it is called when a page argues something the evidence has since outgrown. and three that leave the building. a second roadmap begins at item 51, raised the same evening, and it is mostly the cost of a good day: nine research campaigns opened by things found on 15 september, six more machine checks, seven pages that now argue less than the evidence supports, and four things for the estate and the post. a day that finds a great deal also makes a great deal of work, and pretending otherwise is how a list becomes a monument. a list this long is a risk in itself: the failure mode is not forgetting an item but stopping reading at item 12. anything here that is still untouched in six weeks should be struck rather than carried.

“mr miles” identified — he is the officer who accepted kolbe, not merely the man who carried the news

an inference this archive is publishing as an inference, and would rather have as a document. the letter of 23 august 1830 says only “mr miles had called at our house”. the journal of 25 november 1828 is addressed to the rev. richard miles, superintendent of the society’s missions in africa, and richard miles — formerly pastor of brigg in lincolnshire, originally appointed to demerara — was sent to cape town to act as dr philip’s substitute while philip was in england. the office, the continent and the dates all fit: philip in england from 1826, miles acting at the cape in 1828, philip back and miles in london by 1830. what would settle it is the lms’s own records of its officers — sibree’s register, or the cwm home correspondence at soas, both already on this list. if it holds, the man kolbe reported to from philippolis is the man who knocked on his father’s door. settled 20 september, by sibree’s register. “accepted provisionally by mr. miles, feb. 8, 1829, which action was confirmed by the directors, july 29, 1829.” miles did not carry the news — miles made the decision. and the father’s adverb turns out to be the society’s own vocabulary: provisionally by miles at the cape, confirmed by the directors in london, and a father told his son had been “fully accepted”. richard miles was acting superintendent of the lms at cape town from 1825, standing in for dr philip while philip was in britain. the letter still gives no forename, so the surname is carried by the office and the dates — but the office is now his own.

the mirror story — found: it is fiction, by james hogg, and the tailor was right not to believe it

the father devotes two of his four pages to it and asks his son to say whether it is true. the mirror of literature, amusement, and instruction ran weekly from 1822 and is digitised in several places. the story: a scottish colonist near the xhosa, orang-outangs, a shot young animal that proves to be a chief’s son, a wife carried off, capt johnson and a company of soldiers, and a recovery after nearly two years. it would date to 1829 or the first half of 1830. worth finding for its own sake: it is the only thing this archive has that shows what the london household was reading about africa while its son was living there. 20 september — searched and not found. google books tried on “melvill and kolbe”-style phrasing and on the story’s own terms (“ourang outang” / “orang outang” with carried off, wife, colonist, caffre, mirror, 1829–1830) — no books matches at all — and the same on the open web. recorded so nobody repeats it. next attempts: the runs of the mirror on project gutenberg and the internet archive, searched by volume rather than by phrase, and the distinctive surname williams or williamson with capt johnson. found 21 september, after five failed searches, by downloading the volumes and reading them. the mirror of literature, amusement, and instruction, volume xiv (1829), pp. 313–318: “spirit of the public journals — a singular letter from southern africa. communicated by mr. hogg, the ettrick shepherd.” it is james hogg, author of the private memoirs and confessions of a justified sinner, printed as though it were a settler’s letter home. every detail in the 1830 letter is in it: the chief karoo offering oxen and “a choice virgin to boot” for the settler’s wife; frederick william kolbe — resolved: not the settler’s son. sibree is wrong and schoeman is right

a flat contradiction between two printed authorities, with a chronological impossibility inside it. sibree, entry 522: “kolbe, frederick william. born, nov. 3, 1821, in south africa. son of rev. g. a. kolbe (no. 278). had been connected with the rhenish mission… died at cape town, dec. 25, 1899, aged 78.” author of an english–herero dictionary (juta, 1883), minister at george and then paarl. schoeman: “f.w. kolbe (1821–99) van die rynse sendinggenootskap was nie aan hierdie familie verwant nie.” same man, same society, same years. and he cannot simply be adopted. sibree’s 3 november 1821 agrees with his own age at death; the settler’s known eldest, john gerson eliezar, was born 7 july 1822, and his age at death agrees too. eight months apart. one of the two births is wrong, or one of the men is not who his source says. sibree also gives him a sister — charlotte kolbe, born 25 december 1829, who married rev. william sykes at paarl in 1860; the settler’s 1829 daughter is recorded here under another name. the paper that would settle it is at soas: a missionary’s own candidate papers state his parentage. resolved the same day. three independent works: the new catholic encyclopedia, on his son monsignor f.c. kolbe — “the son of a westphalian (german) protestant missionary who had married the daughter of a member of the london missionary society”; the s2a3 biographical database, which names him friedrich wilhelm kolbe, rhenish missionary and herero scholar, married at cape town in 1849, at okahandja by april 1850, fled to otjikango when jonker afrikaner attacked the hereros that august, back in the colony from 1852 — george, paarl, stellenbosch, cape town; and dsab vol. 5 (hsrc, 1987), which carries its own entry on f.w. kolbe and was in print five years before schoeman wrote. sibree’s register has two kolbes in south africa, 278 and 522, and a compiler joined them. the same species of error as schoeman giving the father the son’s trade. charlotte kolbe, born 25 december 1829, goes with him.
