found elizabetha van der merwe was put to the index three ways — her daughter, her children as a class, and her son's own baptism — and came back empty all three times, which leaves her where she started: one document, the 1908 death notice of her son. then the same method that failed her worked on the barrys. asked for every barry child of a kolbe mother rather than for any particular person, the index returned two names on neither parent's death notice — and an hour later, checking this archive's own files, one of them turned out to have been recorded here all along. that is logged as a correction. the one new name is henry jaonas barry, born 13 july 1848, which is where a next child belongs after a brother born in march 1847. index-only, ambiguous, and familysearch blocked the follow-up before the image could be reached. written down as a lead and not as a child.
withdrawn — “he died in the transvaal at about thirty” taken back

found this archive gave estate tab mhg o/2899 to jan gerhardus lodewicus booysen, born 4 december 1855, the seventh child on the 1863 death notice, and wrote a death date of 1885 into his life on that basis. the date had no source except the file number. the transvaal probate index names the estate's deceased in full: jan gerardus lodewicus booijzen, aged 67, born district graaff-reinet, died 25 may 1885 at vaalbank, district lichtenburg — born about 1818, which is his uncle, fifth on the 1876 sterfkennis. the nephew's death date is withdrawn and nothing is known about what became of him. the particular error is worth naming: the archive read a year off a reference number, wrote it in as a fact, and then cited the fact back.
lichtenburg joins the line found

found the same correction does the opposite favour. vaalbank, in the district of lichtenburg, is where the 1876 man's son died in 1885 — and this archive had already read a 1920 sterfkennis from that farm for magdalena susanna maria van den berg, born booyzen about 1860, father entered as jan gerhardus lodewicus booyzen, filed under “not proved”. she is his daughter. two deaths on one farm thirty-five years apart, which is settlement rather than passage. read west along the atlas: rustenburg 1876, lichtenburg 1885 and 1920, marico 1903. three neighbouring districts, and this archive spent months insisting the third of them was somebody else's family.
the last six transvaal estates are blocked, not missing method

found six estates have sat on the sources page as “located” for weeks, on the assumption that they were simply not name-indexed and would yield to film browsing. they will not. the collection runs on 762 films; every film up to 007830062 serves its images and every film from 007830063 onward returns 403 — twenty-eight tested, twenty-eight refused — and those are precisely the films carrying 1946 and later. five of the six are behind that line. the sixth, 52653 of 1923, is in the open half but is not name-indexed, and the films are not ordered by estate number: image 100 of three films in the same numeric neighbourhood gave a 1920 sterfkennis, a 1938 death notice, and a chinese clan genealogy. there is nothing to interpolate along. the queue moves off the screen and onto a letter to pretoria. one trap recorded on the way: q.filmnumber works as a search term alone and is silently ignored the moment a surname is added, returning a whole-collection result that looks like a film result.
a third letter, to pretoria method

found sent to enquiries2@dsac.gov.za, the research address on the national archives repository's own contact page, copied to the head of client services. six estate files — mhg 1095/48, 3734/46, 769/52, 5155/51, 10/57 and 52653 — with the death notice asked for ahead of the will and the account in each, because six death notices are worth more to this archive than one complete file. their own page states that records older than twenty years carry a public right of access free of charge. whether it was delivered is a separate question from whether it was sent, and this archive will not use the second word until it has checked for the first.
a dead child's name, given again — watched happening found

found worked out of the register rather than off a new document. hercules johannes mountjoy and maria sophia van niekerk baptised a daughter at dordrecht on 6 september 1896 and called her carolina isabella margaretha aletta, her grandmother's four names entire. she died at wodehouse on 25 october 1897, aged fourteen months. on 8 november 1901 they had another daughter and gave her the whole name again; she married hendrik stefanus palm, and a granddaughter born in 1920 carries it still. replacement naming is well attested in these congregations and is exactly how a records-matcher invents one person out of two. the dates here make it unmistakable, and this archive keeps the two apart. five of the eight children of that marriage are named for a parent or a grandparent — the same habit as the barry names crossing into the daschners, seen from the other direction and in another family.
johanna catharina booysen gets her dates found

found second on the 1863 death notice and until now nothing but a position in a list. the dutch reformed index gives her born 15 may 1844 and baptised at brak rivier on 4 august 1844 — the farm her father was still on nineteen years later when her mother died there. a small thing, and the kind the register was built to hand over.
withdrawn — isabella frederika coetsee died in 1943 taken back

found she died on 31 march 1930, at church street, middelburg. 1943 is when her husband finally filed. this archive had taken the year off the estate reference and written it in as a death date — the same error it corrected on o/2899 three days ago, sitting undetected in the next record along. two instances in one week of one habit: trusting a file number to tell you when somebody died. the notice also names her parents, three children, and a son this archive had been carrying as living who was already dead.
the oldest booyzen death notice in the cape — and why it is dangerous found

found death notice 6167, filed cape town 21 june 1843, under section 9 of ordinance 104 — a generation older in form than anything else here. johanna booyzen, born in the colony about 20 march 1754, died 16 june 1843 at 28 roze street, widow of charles du plessis, one daughter married to benjamin solomon, and “no property whatever except a bond amounting per balance to £15”. line 3 reads “both dead” — the seventh failure of that question in this archive and the earliest. she is not this family. she is recorded because the only two dates this archive holds for magdelena elisabeth de beer are born 1754 and died 1843, both off the family tree with no source, and here is a booyzen woman who matches both to the year and is demonstrably somebody else. that is exactly the material a bad merge is made of, and it is better to have met it deliberately than to meet it by accident.
the post, checked method

found three enquiries out, none answered. western cape archives (sent 9 sep, four days): silence. sandf documentation centre (9 sep): one of the two addresses bounced within seconds — 550 5.7.1, relay access denied — and the other has said nothing in four days. national archives, pretoria (12 sep): no bounce, too early for anything else. recorded with the date because silence and inaction are indistinguishable on a page that does not say which it is, and this archive has already had to correct itself once for calling a half-delivered letter sent.
the cape compensation series, named — and then shown to be unsearchable by name method

found open question 11 has asked for “cape colony compensation claims” for weeks without knowing what they were called. they are the war losses compensation commission, 1902 — kab, source na, volume 564, reference a1068. the cape depot holds 454 documents mentioning compensation and war, and 679 mentioning losses. booyzen appears in none of them. that would ordinarily be worth something, and here it is worth very little: smit, schoeman and barry also return nothing, and the two botha hits are a 1935 locust and arsenical-poisoning stock claim from a magistrate's series. the commission is catalogued by sub-commissioner and volume, not by claimant. a name search cannot reach these files, so a name search failing to reach them proves nothing. the question stays open and the way in is the reading room. two working notes recorded with it: the naairs asterisk wildcard returns zero rather than expanding — booy* gives 0 in a depot where booyzen gives 39 — and the bare hostname national.archsrch.gov.za no longer resolves at all, though www.national.archsrch.gov.za does.
not one barry of this family is in the master's index — and the reason is a habit found

found film 007844477 is the cape master's own index of estates 1834–1912: every estate reported in the colony for seventy-eight years, alphabetically, with the death-notice number beside each name. barry runs across pages 232 to 234 and this family is on none of them. no richard peter — which was the point of going, since a richard peter barry of jerpoint is on the cape rebel roll and the estate would have identified him. no frederick fortunatus, no dorothea regina, no hendrik nicholaas, no kathleen mary. and no john augustus, who died in august 1903 in the middle of the index's range, and no margaretha, who died in 1912 as it closed. then the reason arrives and it is not an absence: this archive has read both their death notices and both are dated 29 march 1915, sworn by their sons. the index stops in 1912. john augustus barry died and nobody reported his estate for twelve years. it is the third instance of the same habit here — isabella coetzee died in 1930 and was reported in 1943, maria kumm died in 1934 and was reported in 1938 with “death not reported” typed on the form. three families, three decades, and twice a husband's and a wife's estate filed on the same day by a son. any search that assumes an estate was reported in the year of the death will miss all of them, and two of this archive's own corrections are exactly that mistake.
a mountjoy at indwe, and a barry who carries two families in one name found

found items 5, 10 and 11 of the standing list. the indwe lidmaten register, page 336: johanna catharina mountjoy joined the congregation on 23 july 1907, arriving from barkly oost — six weeks after willem hermanus booijzen was confirmed in the same church — and the last column records her dead at indwe in june 1911. a mountjoy and a booyzen in one small colliery congregation, twenty-two years after the two families stood at the same font at barkly oost. ranking a whole-surname search by place then produced the barkly east barrys: james henry, who swore his father's 1915 notice, dated at last (c.1847 – 23 june 1939); harriet louisa of manorowen, dead at eighteen in 1912; cornelia herculena petronella of cherryville, a third named barry farm after manorowen and jerpoint; and richard pieter kolbe barry, born 1899, who carries the forename of the man on the cape rebel roll and the surname of the 1820 settler family in one name. it does not prove the identification. it does show that whoever named that child was standing inside the family this archive is describing. and a second reason why no barry is in the cape master's index: john barry's 1915 estate was administered at grahamstown, not cape town.
willem hermanus booyzen of indwe stops in 1910 method

found item 5 was to read the indwe registers forward from 1910 for the miner. the dutch reformed index holds nothing further: no third baptism, no marriage after 1908, no death. he is confirmed at 21 in 1907, married at 22 in 1908, has two children by two roodt women in 1908 and 1909, and after his daughter's baptism on 22 september 1910 he is twenty-four years old and gone from the record this archive can reach. recorded as a scoped negative rather than left as an open thread: the index has been asked and has nothing.
“irishman born in ireland” — open question 5, answered found

found entry 74, district barkly east, 28 october 1903: the statutory registration of john barry's death, made by his son richard barry, “son present at death”, of manor owen. question 5, race: “irishman born in ireland”. also: aged eighty-four years two months, so born about june 1819; a carpenter, which is the first trade this archive has for him; resident and dead at manor owen ward iv, which turns out to have been his own house and not merely his son's; dead on 25 august 1903; and the footnote that asks for the number of his children answers eleven, where this archive has named nine. the 1915 death notice this archive had been arguing from — “at sea, exact whereabouts unknown, british” — was sworn by a different son twelve years after the fact. where the two disagree the archive now follows 1903, and that includes the date of death, where the family tree turns out to have been right and the document the archive preferred wrong.
irishman, then dutch, on the same form nine years apart found

found harriet louisa barry died of typhoid at cherryville on 7 september 1912, aged eighteen years five months and three days, and was buried at manorowen. her father hendrik nicholaas barry signed the registration — “father present when died” — and question 5 enters her as “dutch, born in the district of barkly east”. nine years earlier the same printed question, at the same farm, called her grandfather an irishman born in ireland. the family testimony says exactly this in its least-examined line — “as his son and grandson were married to dutch girls their activity during the boer war would be interesting” — and here it is on a government form, taking two generations and nine years.
a mother nobody had, and a marriage at zeerust found

found transvaal estate 14380. hendrik stephanus booysen, who signed his father's sterfkennis at brakfontein in september 1876, died on 11 may 1908 at koedoesfontein in the district of rustenburg, in the house of his son-in-law, aged seventy-nine years eleven months. his own notice names his mother: elizabetha booysen, born van der merwe. that resolves the oldest “serious” contradiction on the disputed page — anna maria van der merwe died before march 1825 and this son was born about june 1828 — and it was never a contradiction, only a missing row: two van der merwe wives, one after the other. it also repairs the warning printed on the 1876 household, which had to draw eight children under one marriage because no other was recorded. and the place of his last marriage is zeerust — the principal town of the district of marico. this archive spent weeks saying of the marico booyzens that they are not this family, and has spent three days walking it back through rustenburg and lichtenburg. here is a son of the 1876 man married in the third district. it still links nobody to the seven compensation claims, and the atlas still says unresolved. the withdrawn sentence was wronger than it knew.
the marriages, the errands, and a register that refused eight surnames method

found the last three items of the standing list. the marriages: eighteen, in order, with the place in the column that matters — three at graaff-reinet and cradock before 1850, fifty years in the north-eastern cape, then vereeniging and johannesburg once and finally. two are hinges: cradock 1838 joins booysen to mountjoy, mayfair 1949 is where this archive stops. errands: four doors, twenty things that could be settled behind them, every reference written out — pretoria for six blocked estates, roeland street for two mountjoy wills and the war losses commission registers that no name search can reach, grahamstown for a depot discovered today and never searched, and barkly east for four farms and three churches that exist here only as film. the register: refreshed, and it grew by the reconstructed people rather than by harvest. eight in-law surnames were pulled and all eight rejected — keys 1,199, grobelaar 726, dormehl 1,841, palm 3,818, siebert 3,613, buitendag 7,686, roodt 12,916 and olivier 81,327. four hundred of eighty-one thousand chosen by a search engine's idea of relevance is not a sample of anything, and the page says so beside the counts.
the 1915 notice, read past the fourth line taken back

found this archive has shown the top of john barry's 1915 death notice for weeks and quoted four lines from it — the birthplace, the mother's maiden name, the signature. the children's list is further down the page and had never been read. it names eight: john augustus, james henry, george augustus (new), henry nicholas, frederick fortunatus, richard peter, margaret mary bedford and kathleen mary boyson, born barry, married in community of property to william boyson — the only booyzen marriage on the list, spelled boyson by an english clerk. dorothea regina and ruben jacobus josuah are not on it, and this archive had both as children “named on the 1915 death notice”. they are grandchildren: a dorothea regina baptised at slang river in 1892 and a ruben jacobus hosea at dordrecht in 1888, both to henry nicholas barry and anna johanna maria schoeman. the page also gives margaretha kolbe's death as 2 august 1912, where this archive had only the year. and it says the marriage took place at “burghersdorp (probably)” — a son of the house, writing in english with a solicitor's help, who did not know where his parents married and put it in brackets.

found the 1903 registration answers the printed question “the total number of children deceased has had” with eleven. the 1915 death notice names eight. three children of john barry and margaretha kolbe died before 1915 and this archive cannot name one of them. it is the first hard count of that generation it has ever had, and it is three short.
the ancestor chart had every wife one generation too high taken back

found the tree page has been drawing each man's wife in his mother's box since it was built — four slots, all shifted by one, and the woman at the root of the whole chart had no mother drawn at all. rebuilt. the slot that is genuinely empty, the mother of the 1812 man, is now a fifth wall marked disputed: a family tree supplies anna maria van der merwe and no document does.
a drift checker, and the three things it found in its first run method

found tools/drift.py now runs in build.sh beside tools/links.py and fails the build when a narrative page contradicts the data. its first real run found the pedigree missing two documented wives, the direct line showing one wife where kin.js has two, and two men named in a household who had no page at all. a family history that only shows its conclusions is asking to be believed on trust; a build that will not publish a contradiction is cheaper than another month of reading by eye.
1892 — the zeerust marriage, and four children move mother found

found the 1908 death notice said the last marriage was at zeerust and nothing more. the register gives entry 13 on 14 april 1892: hendrik stefanus booijzen, 63, weduwnaar of brakfontein in rustenburg, and charlotta elizabeth roos born dormehl, 51, weduwe of driefontein in marico, both born at graaff-reinet. three things follow. his birthplace is now a town and not a colony, and it is the same town as three other men of this line. he was still at brakfontein sixteen years after he signed his father's sterfkennis there. and his four children cannot be hers: she was fifty-one at the wedding and they were adults by 1908, so they belong to the first wife, anna catharina johanna olivier. the clerk writes him booijzen; he signs himself booysen.
brakfontein, 1891 — a wife, a son, and two of this archive's own misreadings found

found a week ago this site found a woman it called anna johanna booijzen, born alberts, who died in 1891 at boekfontein in the district of rustenburg, and filed her under not proved to be kin. read at full resolution the farm is brakfontein — the farm where the oldest document on this site was written in 1876 and where hendrik stefanus still lived in 1892 — and the maiden name is oliefier, which has no b, no r, no t and no s in it. her son gives olivier on the 1908 notice. she is anna catharina johanna olivier, the first wife, and her death notice lists seven children where the 1908 notice named four. two of them were new. so was her son hendrick stefanus nicolaas, twenty-nine, unmarried, dead on the same farm five days after her. so were her parents, ocken johannes oliefier and anna johanna botha — which is at last where ockert johannes came into this family. every one of those facts was on a page this archive had already found.
the rustenburg register confirms olivier from a third direction found

found an hour after reading oliefier off a death notice and arguing it was olivier, the netherdutch reformed church register of rustenburg said so outright. a baptism of 25 december 1862 gives a boy born 31 january 1862 to hendrik stephanus booijsen and anna johanna olivier — and 31 january 1862 is a date this archive did not have but had calculated, from 29 jaar 3 maanden en 14 dagen on a torn 1891 notice. they agree to the day. the same register admits two brothers to membership on one sunday in april 1869, petrus jacobus born 20 april 1851 and ockert johannes stephanus born 15 september 1852, and baptises a nephew in 1882 named for the uncle who would die at brakfontein. ockert himself died at klerksdorp on 16 january 1921, aged sixty-nine. every one of these entries is index only — familysearch has no image for any of them — and they are published on their own page for that reason.
the second willem hermanus, followed to the end found

found he was a name with a beginning and no end: a lidmaat at indwe in 1907, a mijnwerker on two baptisms, a marriage known only from an index, and nothing after 1910. the indwe register page has now been read — entry 13, 21 september 1908, he twenty-two and a mijnwerker, she sixteen and marrying with her parents' consent, both of dugmore mijn, and their son already four months old and not baptised until december. and the end of him: a william herman booyzen, 47, born cape province, married, ex miner underground, of 62 langford street in booysens, dead at johannesburg hospital on 29 july 1932 of a perforated duodenal ulcer after about one day, buried at brixton on the 31st. his father died of a stomach ulcer at indwe in 1905. familysearch indexes the age as 44; the form says 47 and the burial register agrees with the form. read the image, not the index — the third time today.

found a direct-line ancestor has had two bare years on this site since it was built: catherine maria sophia “kathleen” barry, 1859–1940. the city of johannesburg burial register gives the rest — buried 6 september 1940 at the new cemetery (brixton), aged 82, section d.r., grave 9760. it is the first grave number this archive has for anybody, and it is one a family could walk to.
charlotta's own notice, and the same answer from the other side found

found this morning the 1892 zeerust register made it impossible for hendrik stefanus booysen's four children to be his second wife's: she was fifty-one at the wedding. her own death notice now says it outright. death notice 844, filed september 1902: charlotta elizabetta booysen, born dormehl, dead at driefontein in groot marico on 6 february 1902, aged 60 years 4 months — three husbands, jacob van staden then matthys roos then booysen, and six children, two van stadens and four rooses, and not one booysen. her father was jacob dormehl; her mother is entered unknown, by a husband of ten years, which makes seven death notices in this archive that fail to name a parent. she had one wagon and her furniture, worth £51 8s 0d, and she left a will.
looking for ockert's estate and finding his son's found

found ockert johannes stephanus booysen died at klerksdorp on 16 january 1921 and has no estate file of his own in the indexed transvaal probate records. searched under ockert, okkert, ocker and ocken against booysen, booyzen and booijsen: six hits, every one of them him as somebody else's relative — four duplicate copies of a 1935 sterfkennis where he is the father, and two of his own father's 1908 notice where he is entered child. but the 1935 one is worth the search. sterfkennis 87882, the first afrikaans document in this archive: diederik arnoldus booysen, karweier of zwartruggens, dead at voorbedacht no. 401 in the district of rustenburg on 1 march 1935 — and line 3 names both parents, ockert johannes stephanus booysen and elizabeth johanna sophia gebore myburgh. that couple came into this archive this morning off a rustenburg baptism index with no image, published with a warning saying so. here they are on a page that can be read. and their grandson, born 23 october 1927, is the fourth generation to carry a name that came in from the district of cradock with one marriage.
grave 6889 closes the second willem hermanus found

found the 1932 identification was built on circumstance — ex miner underground, born cape province, married, forty-seven, brixton. the johannesburg grave register settles it. grave 6889 holds “boysen, william”, folio 49, and beneath him susanna adriana booyzen, buried 29 august 1968. susanna adriana roodt is the sixteen-year-old he married at indwe on 21 september 1908. husband and wife in one grave, thirty-six years apart. and the clerk spells him boysen — the same spelling an english clerk used for a different man of this family on john barry's 1915 death notice.
the olivier line, and a marriage that moves the whole family twenty-six years found

found yesterday anna catharina johanna olivier did not exist on this site. this morning she was recovered from a death notice the archive had misread twice. this afternoon there are two more documents. her baptism: cradock, 4 october 1824, born 10 september, father ockert johannes stephanus olivier — all three names, exactly what her son was called — and mother anna catharina botha; with a sister aletta catharina baptised in the same church eleven months before, which is where her own daughter's name comes from. and her marriage: potchefstroom, 3 july 1850, entry 206, hendrik stephanus booijzen 23 and anna johanna olivier 25 — her maiden name written plainly by a clerk who could write, forty-one years before the scrawl this archive read as alberts. the marriage is the thing. this site began by saying the family went north by railway in the twentieth century; the 1876 sterfkennis moved that to rustenburg in 1876; this moves it to potchefstroom in 1850, two years before the sand river convention. a booijzen was standing in a transvaal church before there was a transvaal.
ten index entries, one death notice, and the direct line's own brother found

found a run of ten entries under booijzen in the transvaal probate index carried no dates, no places and nothing to identify them. they are all one document: death notice 4795, for elizabetha margaretha booijzen born marais, who died on 1 june 1900 in a zinc building in market street, pretoria — four days before lord roberts entered the town — and whose husband did not file it until march 1904. her husband is david schalk booijzen, born 9 june 1848: fourth on the 1863 death notice of johanna catharina mountjoy, where willem hermanus of the direct line is sixth. his brother. they married at lady grey near aliwal north, the same small cape church where willem hermanus married kathleen barry in 1879. eight children, one squeezed in between the lines with died minor against her. nothing movable, and a compensation claim filed — which takes back a negative this archive published about the war losses compensation commission. and it unsettles an inference: the notice names a stephanus francois booijzen as their son, and this site has a stephanus francois booyzen of 1874 placed under a different father on his birth date alone.
the burial registers, swept — and black october found

found grave 9760 took twenty minutes, so the whole johannesburg cemetery collection was read: 298 entries under six surnames. ten are this family, and each turns a year the archive was carrying into a day. henry james booyzen had been a name on estate mhg 10/57 with no birth and no death; he died 8 december 1956 aged 69. joseph heinrich daschner was buried at west park on 21 april 1942. hendrik stephanus nicolaas booyen, found this morning as a rustenburg baptism and a kempton park death, was buried at johannesburg on 12 october 1959. and two infants at brixton the archive did not have at all. then october 1918. richard peter booyzen, twenty-four, buried at brixton on the 27th — the centre of black october. this archive has no richard peter booyzen and it should: richard peter barry is kathleen's own brother, and a boy born about 1894 falls exactly in the gap between her daughter of 1891 and her son of 1901. added as a ninth child, marked inferred, because a burial register names no parents. two more booysens went into the same ground within eight weeks and neither can be shown to be kin.
estate 1291, and a ninth barry child found

found this archive looked for margaretha kolbe's estate on the films either side of 925, her husband's, and did not find it. it is 1291, and it is indexed under cape, kimberley, probate records of the supreme court while the probate itself was granted at grahamstown. a collection label and a place that disagree is exactly how a record hides. death notice 1291: margaret louisa elizabeth barry born kolbe, 84, afrikander of european extraction, dead on 2 august 1912 in the house of her son r. p. barry at manorowen, leaving no movable property, no immovable property, estate nil and no will. and question ten names nine children where her husband's notice names eight. the ninth is william, who is on nothing else in this archive. “eight is not eleven” becomes “nine is not eleven”. two other things: her son puts his father's death in august 1904 when the registration says 25 august 1903, and where his parents were married he writes unknown — three months before writing “burghersdorp (probably)” on his father's. two documents by one man in one year, and he cannot place his own parents' wedding on either.
eight mountjoy children, the keys question closed, and four honest noes found

found george mountjoy and maria sophia botha married at cradock in 1848 and had thirteen children; this archive could name one. the baptism registers name eight, and the places track the family across the border — graaff-reinet 1858, burgersdorp 1860, smithfield in the orange free state 1862 and 1864. one of the eight answers an open question: johanna catharina mountjoy, baptised at burgersdorp on 29 february 1860, a leap day, is the woman who married william henry keys and put mountjoy forenames into a third surname. a petronella christina aletta baptised at swellendam in 1871 carries both parents' names and is not adopted: swellendam is six hundred miles west of anywhere else this family stood. and four questions answered no: elizabetha van der merwe's marriage is not in any index, so the eight children of 1876 stay under their warning; the five remaining 1876 children have no document of their own; ockert johannes stephanus booysen has no estate file; and the three untraced daughters of 1891 stay untraced — this archive will not decide that the anna catharina grobelaar of 1908 is the anna johanna maria of 1891, because the forenames do not agree and guessing that they do is the exact mistake it spent today undoing.
marico: the initials still fail, and the reason for dismissing them is gone taken back

found in september this archive set aside seven tab cjc compensation claims from marico with the sentence “that is not this family, who were cape”, and could not test the initials because it could not name a single grandson. it can name them now, and the test still fails — of jpj, pj, gl, jpj, l, jc and he only pj fits, and petrus jacobus is the commonest name this family has. but the sentence is false twice over. hendrik stefanus booijzen married at zeerust, the principal town of marico, on 14 april 1892; and his wife died at driefontein, groot marico on 6 february 1902, during the war, in the district the claims come from. the claims are still not tied to a named man. what has gone is the excuse for not looking.
a page that says what moved method

found this archive is rewritten most days and a reader who saw it last week had no way of knowing what changed. /changes/ is that record: every finding and every withdrawal, grouped by the day it happened, newest first. it is built from log.json and corrections.json at build time and contains no hand-written text, so it cannot go stale the way a “latest news” box always does. if a finding is not on it, it is not in the log.
the post, chased — and the sandf address is not the problem method

found three letters out, no replies and no new bounces. pretoria (sent today, six transvaal estate files): delivered, no bounce, too early for anything else. western cape archives (two letters, 9 september — the mountjoy wills and the lerena death notice): delivered, four days, silent. sandf (9 september): the mweb address bounced with “relay access denied” and archive@dod.mil.za delivered. re-checked today: the stellenbosch library guide, updated 1 september 2026, no longer lists the mweb address at all — it gives archive@dod.mil.za and nothing else. so there is no better address to switch to; the one that bounced is a dead address that third-party sites keep republishing. the same guide shows the centre has moved, from the schweikert building at 20 visagie street to 42 saturnus road, irene — the national archives directory still has the old one. and it names two officers for paia requests, which carries a statutory duty to answer. if archive@dod.mil.za is still silent on 7 october, that is the next step, and not another general enquiry.
a marriage register that cites an estate number found

found this archive lost the direct ancestor's brother in march 1904, signing his wife's death notice at pretoria. he turns up nineteen months later in the same city, marrying again: entry 105, 27 november 1905, david schalk booyzen, 56, widower, born cradock, of goede hoop, pretoria, to johanna elena lowies born stols, 51, a widow of skinners court. the remarks column reads “remarriage certificate from master supreme court no. 4795 dated 4/11/05” — and 4795 is the estate number of the death notice this archive read an hour earlier, for elizabetha margaretha booijzen born marais, dead in a zinc building in market street in 1900. the master would not let a widower remarry until the first estate was in order, and the marriage clerk wrote the estate number down. the two documents cite each other. it is also a method: the remarks column of a transvaal civil marriage register carries the master's estate number whenever a widow or widower remarries, which indexes marriages to estate files in the direction this archive usually cannot go — from somebody alive to a file about somebody dead. and it gives him a birthplace: cradock. his death is still not found.
william, found — and the two kolbe sisters on one page found

found this morning william barry existed on one line of his mother's 1915 death notice and nowhere else. the burgersdorp doopregister has his baptism: william fredrik, entry 2187, born 23 august 1853, christened 23 october, father john barry, mother margareth kolbe — with godparents john kolbe, anna van der merwe and george kolbe, two of whom are his mother's brothers and none of whom this archive had. and the entry two lines above it is the other thing. 2186, the same afternoon: augustus kolbe, father george fredk enslin, mother mary elizabeth kolbe. this site carried a contradiction marked serious — margaretha kolbe appearing to marry enslin while married to john barry — and resolved it from margaret downing's 1867 death notice, which named a daughter mary elizabeth married to george f. enslin. here are the two sisters, baptising a son each, two entries apart, on one page. six more baptisms from the same registers give exact birth dates to five barry children, including the direct ancestor: catherina mary sophia barry, born 4 august 1859, who has been “1859” on this site since it was built.
three graves read off the register, and one of them is the direct line found

found grave 2171, dutch reformed section, west park — george downing mountjoy booyzen, 46, buried 14 december 1947. this archive has had “buried west park 14 dec” since it was built and never the number. and a double plot: joseph heinrich daschner, 58, buried 21 april 1942 in grave 50 of a pair 50/51 he bought himself, with a memorial by l. canata & son — and the consecutive grave-number register braces 50 and 51 together, daschner joseph h. and daschner catherine m.s. she is catharina maria sophia booysen, born 22 april 1891 at barkly oost, george's own sister, whose estate mhg 3734/46 is one of the six files in the letter to pretoria. four years after he was buried in the first grave she went into the second. the family lies in three graves across two cemeteries: kathleen barry at brixton in 9760, her son willem hermanus and his wife at brixton in 6889, her son george at west park in 2171, and her daughter and son-in-law at west park in 50 and 51.
a drift check for the atlas, and three shared names verified by eye method

found six farms and towns were written into /documents/ today before places.json had heard of any of them — potchefstroom, zeerust, driefontein, zwartruggens, voorbedacht no. 401, klerksdorp and market street. all six are now in the atlas, and tools/drift.py fails the build if a place named in a timeline event is not in places.json. tested against a deliberate miss before it was trusted. separately, the shared-name warning was worked through by eye and all three are genuinely two or three people: george mountjoy the saddler of 1823 and the child baptised at barkly oost in 1889; three petrus jacobus booysens of 1788, 1812 and 1839, father to son to grandson; and two willem hermanus pieterzens, the one dead before 1817 who was anna catharina sleer's first husband, and his son who stood godfather at the 1851 font. none is one person entered twice.
a good theory, killed by its own document taken back

found richard peter booyzen came into this archive at lunchtime off a burial register as an inferred ninth child. his death registration makes the identification firmer and destroys the best idea this archive had about his mother. firmer: 18 anderson street, turffontein; twenty-four; born at the cape of good hope, which is the migration every one of kathleen barry's children made; dead of influenza and pneumonia after eleven days on 25 october 1918. destroyed: this site has been asking for months why kathleen barry was a military pensioner at her death, and saying that no son of hers is among the first world war dead. a son dead in october 1918 looked like the answer — huge numbers of south african servicemen died in that epidemic and their dependants were pensioned. he was not a soldier. occupation: sawyer. condition: married, so there is a widow, and a married son's death does not pension his mother anyway. the theory is rejected and the open question is now better specified: the pension belongs to a son who served and survived, which is exactly what the letter already at the sandf documentation centre asks about. three other johannesburg booyzens were tested and none is claimed — petrus jacobus of 1882 (a name and a gap and no document), petrus jacobus van blerk booyzen (no van blerk in this family), and jan gerhardus lodewikus buried in 1943 (right name, no age, too common). john zacharia booysen of the same influenza weeks is rejected outright: zacharia reaches nothing here.
two questions worked hard and not closed method

found both were predicted to fail before they were started. one did. stephanus francois booyzen's marriage register at mosselbaai — 5 september 1905, certificate 1318 — has a column for woonplaats and none for waar geboren, and no column for parents at all, so it cannot decide whose son he was. but it tilts: he is thirty, a jonkman, a metselaar, and his residence is pretoria — and eleven weeks later david schalk booijzen of goede hoop, pretoria, whose 1900 notice names an unmarried major son called stephanus françois, married again in that same city. still marked serious. this archive is not going to decide a father on a city. the other moved further than expected. ockert johannes stephanus olivier and anna catharina botha married at graaff-reinet on 8 december 1816 — index only, no image — and have four children baptised at cradock between 1820 and 1826: gert cornelis, aletta catharina, anna johanna and an ockert johannes stephanus the younger. graaff-reinet is the booysens' own town. the two families were in the same place at the same time and their children married each other six hundred miles north at potchefstroom in 1850. what is still not done is the thing that was asked: this archive still cannot tell this ockert johannes stephanus olivier from the ockert johannis fredrik lodewyk, the okker petrus jacobus and the ockert johannes frederik baptising at cradock in the same decade. her line still stops with her parents.
the other number on the same line found

found the pretoria marriage register of 27 november 1905 cites two remarriage certificates from the master, one per party. 4795 was the groom's and led back to his first wife's death notice. 7081 is the bride's, and it is charles petrus barend lowies — born in the district of cradock about 1849, dead at pretoria on 5 june 1905, parents jan lowies and elisabetha maria lubbe, twelve children. read the two men together: david schalk booijzen born cradock 9 june 1848 and widowed at pretoria in 1900; charles petrus barend lowies born district cradock about 1849 and dead at pretoria in 1905. two men born a year apart in one karoo district, both ending in pretoria — and five months and twenty-two days after the second died, the first married his widow. the master cleared both estates within four days: 4795 on 4 november, 7081 on the 7th, the wedding on the 27th. between them those two certificates protect eight booijzen children and twelve lowies children. two estate numbers on one line of one register have now produced two death notices, two households and four generations, and this archive has been reading marriage registers for names and dates and skipping the last column. not read: the 7081 file itself. familysearch began refusing record-page requests part-way through — access denied, error 15 — so this is index-level and says so.
eleven children, and a third point in the stephanus francois argument found

found his 1940 estate names eleven children and this site had none of them: david schalk, susanna fredrika aletta (luus), elizabeth magrieta (bekker), beatrix magdalena catharina (vermeulen), johanna catharina (du plessis), ewert philippus, stephanus francois, willem hendrik, petrus jacobus, johan abraham frederik and hendrik rudolph philippus. two of them settle how this couple named: ewert philippus and susanna fredrika aletta are called straight after his wife's parents, evert philip boshoff and susanna frederika aletta meyer, named on her 1890 baptism at mossel bay. so they did name children after grandparents — which makes the eldest son worth looking at. he is called david schalk. if stephanus francois is david schalk booijzen's son, as the 1900 pretoria death notice says, that boy carries his grandfather's name outright; under the parentage this archive published instead, he carries a great-uncle's. a third point for the new reading, and still not proof. added to the disputed row, which stays serious. also: beatrix magdalena catharina boshoff was born 16 june 1889 and baptised at mossel bay on 16 february 1890 — she was sixteen when she married.
anna maria van der merwe stops being a rumour found

found the ancestor chart was rebuilt this morning with a fifth wall against her, marked disputed, and the reason printed beside it was “only a family tree puts her here”. that is no longer true. a dutch reformed baptism names david schalk booijzen, born 12 december 1806 and christened 4 january 1807, as the son of pieter jacobus booijzen and anna maria van der merwe — with an explicit couple relationship between the parents, not two names near each other on a page. and david schalk is first of the eight on the 1876 sterfkennis, which this archive has never had a date for. a son born in december 1806 to a father baptised in september 1788 is a man of eighteen becoming a father, which is exactly what this site has always said. it also resolves a dispute marked serious since the first week: the tree marries them in 1805 and familysearch carries a 1825 cape town marriage of the same two names, and the archive refused to guess which was right. a child born in 1806 settles it — they were married by then, so the 1825 record is a different couple. what is still not proved is that she is the mother of the 1812 man in the direct line, so the wall stays; only its reason has changed. also found: petrus jacobus booijsen, born 29 may 1873 and baptised at lady grey, son of david schalk booijsen and elizabeth margaritha marais — the eldest of the eight on the 1900 pretoria notice, now with a date, in the same church where his uncle married six years later.
the last six graves, and three things this archive had wrong found

found familysearch answered again, so the six register images left unread were read. all ten of this family's johannesburg burials now have a grave number or a section: anna j. mary 2472, john barry 2951, richard peter 1119, george downing daschner 4410, henry james 7110/1, kathleen barry 9760, willem hermanus and susanna adriana 6889, george downing mountjoy 2171, joseph heinrich daschner 50 and catharina maria sophia 51. and three corrections. anna j. mary booyzen lived six months and george downing daschner three months and five days — the index says “0 days” for both because the register keeps years, months and days in three columns and collapses them into one field, and this archive printed the index reading this afternoon without opening the page. neither child was stillborn, and hers was a bought grave. hendrik stephanus nicolaas booysen was buried at roodepoort, not johannesburg — the collection is titled johannesburg cemetery records and the index repeats that label for every register inside it, including other municipalities'. the collection title is not the place. and henry james booyzen, who had no birth and no death this morning, now has everything: dead 8 december 1956 at the florence nightingale nursing home of coronary pulmonary sclerosis, aged 69, of 3 15th avenue, mayfair — the suburb where his mother died in 1940 and his great-niece married in 1949, and which this archive has never had as an address.
estate 7081 read, and the address is the point found

found this archive published estate 7081 from the index a few hours ago and said at the time that the image had not been opened. it is opened now, and it is not the document that was expected. charles petrus barend lowies, a hawker, of goedehoop, pretoria — dead on 5 june 1905 in the lunatic asylum at pretoria, aged 56 years and 8 months, dutch, born in the district of cradock, leaving twelve children of whom six were still minors, movables but no land, and a will. goedehoop is the whole point. it is the exact address david schalk booyzen gave on the marriage register three weeks later — this archive read that register first and wrote down “a widower of goede hoop, pretoria” without knowing what it meant. the two men lived in the same place, and were born in the same cape district within four months of each other. david schalk did not marry a widow from across the town; he married the widow of a man from his own address. she signed the notice on 27 october and married him on 27 november. the index gave the name, the district, the parents and the twelve children; it did not give goedehoop, the asylum, the trade or the eight months on his age.
two more honest noes, once familysearch answered again method

found david schalk booysen, born 9 june 1848, is alive and fifty-six at goedehoop, pretoria on 27 november 1905 and this archive loses him there. no estate file in the indexed transvaal probate records — the only david schalk booyzen in them is a child on the 1940 stephanus francois estate. no civil death that can be him: a cradock man born 1870, a rustenburg man born 1859, a pretoria man born 1907, a clayville man born 1889. the nearest is eleven years out and is not adopted. and the 1876 eight stay at one. searched by mother and by father across 1806 to 1830 in every south african collection: exactly one child of petrus jacobus booysen and anna maria van der merwe is indexed, and it is david schalk of december 1806. the other seven exist on the 1876 sterfkennis and nowhere else.
the twelve lowies children, and the last uncaptioned image method

found estate 7081 named twelve children and this site had none of them: jan jacobus, johanna elena, gabriel jacobus, carl petrus barend, willem jacobus, gideon daniel rudolph and elizabetha maria as majors; matthys andries, radolph lodewyk, abel hermanus gerhardus, lourens daniel albertus and johannes jacobus as minors. three carry the grandparents' names straight through and one her mother's. none of them is a booysen and none is kin — they are here because david schalk booysen became their stepfather a month after their mother signed that page, and because six of them under age are the reason the master made her wait for a remarriage certificate. the same was done this morning for charlotta dormehl's six roos and van staden step-children. and the last unplaced image is placed: detail-1843-age-89.jpg has been sitting in the gallery without a caption or a page since it was cut. it belongs on the 1843 johanna booyzen notice, against the age given to the day — 89 years, 2 months and 26 days — which is the reading that puts her birth at about 20 march 1754 and is exactly why that notice is dangerous: 1754 and 1843 are the only two dates this archive has for magdelena elisabeth de beer, and they came off a tree with no source. every image on the site now has a caption and a page.
the last route to david schalk's death, closed method

found a widow's death notice names her pre-deceased husband, so johanna elena stols — who married david schalk booysen at pretoria in november 1905 — was the last way to date his death. searched under booyzen, booysen and lowies for any death between 1906 and 1945. nothing that can be her. the route is closed rather than untried: neither david schalk booysen nor his second wife has a findable death, and the direct ancestor's brother disappears at goedehoop, pretoria, aged fifty-six, in november 1905. it has been added to the pretoria errand — not as another file request, because the letter is already sent, but as an index search: the master's own estate index at pretoria would settle it in a minute, and that office certainly knew the pair, having handled estates 4795 and 7081 for them within four days of each other.
a way into the documents page method

found /documents/ is now thirty-four documents and 354 kilobytes of html, eighteen of them added today, and a reader arriving at it had no way in and no idea what was there. worse, the sections sat in the order they were written — 1906, then 1942, then 1876, then 1937 — which is the order this archive happened to read them and of no use to anybody else. there is now a contents table at the top, in the order the events happened, and it is read out of the page's own source at build time: the h2 headings are matched, the year is pulled off the front of each, and they are sorted. a section cannot be added without appearing in the contents, for the same reason the gallery is built from the pages rather than written by hand — anything maintained separately goes stale, and this archive has spent the day proving it. three headings that had no year were given one, and the only two entries left undated are the two that genuinely have no date: what was searched and not found, and the two questions worked hard and not closed.

found seven attorney-general files about one police constable at middelburg, 1904–07, spell him booysen four times and booyzen three — twice both ways inside 1905. so the clerk's booysen on the 1905 death form is not an older spelling being displaced; it is what a cape clerk might write on any day. what survives is the half that was always stronger: the son signed, and chose the z.
corrected — the whole project searched one province out of nine taken back

found every naairs search in this archive was run against the cape depot. this family left the cape about 1907 and the entire last generation died in johannesburg, so their estates are in the transvaal — and naairs offers an “all archives repositories” database on the same selection page i used every time. booyzen returns 39 in the cape and 184 across all repositories. one hundred and forty-five documents unseen, including the estate files of nearly everyone in the last three generations.
the johannesburg generation's estates, found found

found anna pretorius (1944), george downing mountjoy booyzen (1947), john barry booyzen (1952), henry james booyzen (1956) — and catharina maria sophia, the daughter baptised at barkly oost in 1891, who married a daschner and died in 1946. also two of the eight children on the 1863 death notice, and both sons of the second marriage.
the 1820 voyage confirmed — and a second lie found under it found

found every date the tree carried for the nautilus is right. the settler roll adds an occupation nobody had — chemist — and two ages: “kolbe, george augustus 20. w margaret 19.” they were sixteen and sixteen. with the 1819 marriage allegation, where both swore twenty-one at sixteen and fifteen, that is two age overstatements in one year on two official documents.

found no estate file for willem hermanus booyzen in any repository in south africa — he died at indwe in 1905 leaving nothing to administer, as his father had in 1884. and nothing supports the mines: no booyzen mining record anywhere in the index, and every occupation actually read for these men points elsewhere — mason, tree nurseryman, railway clerk.
a fourth death notice fails at the same line found

found stephanus francois booyzen's 1940 sterfkennis was fetched for one reason — he was a son of the second marriage, so his mother should be on line 3. his widow wrote “oorlede” for both parents. four death notices in this family now ask who the parents were, and four fail. he was a messelaar, a mason, like his half-brother willem hermanus at indwe.
the second wife, named — johanna margaritha pretorius found

found the oldest open question in the archive, answered by a christening rather than a death. every attempt had gone at death notices, which either do not ask for a wife's name or got “oorlede” for an answer. a baptism names both parents: gert jacobus, born 19 january 1870 — the exact date on the 1884 death notice — baptised 19 june 1870, “oud: petrus jacobus booyzen en johanna margaritha pretorius.” read from the register image, not the index. and two children of the first marriage stood godparent to the first child of the second.
the one death notice where line 3 works found

found tab mhg 2945/44, read at full resolution off the film. anna johanna maria booyzen, born pretorius, died forest hill 26 february 1944, aged 37. the parents line — blank or evasive on all four earlier notices in this archive — is filled in completely: petrus jacobus pretorius and margareth wilhelmina elizabeth pretorius, both at 96 james street, germiston. the form did not change. the person filling it in did. her husband signed it, and her parents were alive and reachable.

found this archive carried margaretha wilhelmina elizabeth “maggie” booyzen’s birth as 1 october 1926, taken from the family tree. her mother’s 1944 death notice, written and signed by her father three months before he lost her, gives 14 october 1926. every other child’s date on that list matches what the archive already held, which is what makes the one mismatch worth taking seriously. corrected to 14 october.
a marriage place, and eleven cousins found

found tab mhg 1928/42 — joseph heinrich daschner's death notice, opened only to put a document behind a marriage the family tree asserted. it gave the marriage (“catherine mary sophia daschner (born booyzen)”), the place (“indwe, cape colony” — the same village where her father died in 1905), his birthplace and parents, and eleven children by name. five of the eleven carry booyzen and barry forenames: catherine mary sophia, margaret wilhelmina elizabeth, william herman, richard peter, henry james. the surname leaves in one generation; the names do not.
withdrawn — “the one time the form worked” taken back

found published this morning, about the 1944 sterfkennis: the one death notice in this archive whose question three names both parents. the very next document opened, the 1942 daschner notice, names both parents too. the claim was a count, and the count was of documents read rather than documents that exist — the oldest mistake in this project. what replaced it is better: question three fails when the informant is remembering the nineteenth-century cape interior, and works when a twentieth-century spouse is writing down in-laws they had actually met. 1840, 1884, 1915 and 1940 fail; 1942 and 1944 work.
the oldest document in this archive — and the two names above the line found

found sterfkennis no. 678, written at the farm brakfontein, district rustenburg, on 14 september 1876. petrus jacobus booijsen, born graaffreinet, aged 88, landbouwer, widower, died 1 september 1876. line 3: “gerthardus lödewikus booijsen — magdalena de beer.” generation seven has stood at the head of the direct line since this archive began with the flattest entry on the site — no dates, no parents, no document. he has a document now. it does not name his own parents, so the oldest open question stays open; it moves him and his wife out of the family tree and into the record, and it retires a 1793 cape will that had made the booysen–de beer pairing look unsafe. the notice also lists eight children, seven of them previously unknown here, and reports the whole estate as “niets nagelaten. niets bekend.”
withdrawn — “they are not this family” taken back

found the atlas said of the marico booyzens: “they are not this family. this one was in the cape until about 1907, and reached the transvaal by railway rather than by commando.” the second sentence is false and the first was resting on it. the direct ancestor died in district rustenburg in 1876 — twenty-five years before the war, a generation before the railway. rustenburg is not marico and no document links this family to any of the seven compensation claims; but the reason for holding the two clusters apart has gone. the map now says unresolved. this is the fifteenth thing this archive has had to take back, and the pattern is consistent: every one of them was a confident negative built on an assumption nobody had tested.
a whole estate, from the death to the last shilling found

found kab mooc 6/9/5047, estates 58379 and 58380 — on the sources page as “located, not yet read” for months. read now, and not only the death notices: the liquidation account and the distribution account too, which is the first time this archive has seen a life in this family added up. james john mountjoy, retired builder of barkly east, died 22 december 1937 aged 83 years 6 months, leaving £664 11s 8d in the post office savings bank, a house on lot 380 let at £2 10s a month, and £400 out on note at six per cent. ten children and two grandchildren took £21. 4. 5. each. his wife’s death, three and a half years earlier, is recorded on his form in four words: “death not reported.” her age gives the only birth date this archive has for her. and the file contradicts itself — his death notice answers question 14 “joint will with predeceased wife”, and the executors’ account four months later opens “the deceased died intestate.” recorded, not resolved.
the false positive, opened found

found hercules johannes mountjoy has no estate file — a negative this archive has stated for months on the strength of a name search. reading the entire indexed mountjoy surname in the cape probate collection at once, 61 personas, produced exactly one hit for him, and it is his mother-in-law’s 1902 death notice from dordrecht: his name appears on it because he is written into her list of eleven children. the negative holds, and now it is understood rather than merely asserted. it also documents the van niekerks: maria sophia van niekerk’s parents, her ten siblings, and a mother born in the district of cradock.
the register — 7,397 entries, and most of them are not this family method

found built to match the sibling archives, which have carried one for a while: every named individual this archive has found, one row for every source that names them. fourteen spellings pulled whole out of familysearch's south african collections — booyzen complete at 1,350, mountjoy at 575, pieterzen at 236, daschner at 46. two were deliberately left alone: booysen returns 40,592 people in this country and barry 7,198, and a name that common fills a page without telling anyone anything. three of the counts are findings in their own right. booyzen 1,350 against booysen 40,592 is the scale behind everything this archive says about the name. and schleher — the family tree's spelling of anna catharina's surname — returns nothing at all, against 851 for slier and 7 for sleer.
every person page now draws its family, and says whose word it is on method

found brought into line with the sibling archives. 110 of the 119 person pages now open with a lineage chart — parents, the person and their spouses, the children of each marriage, and the siblings — and every box is colour-coded by how it is known: the direct line, a record this archive has read, an inference from a record, or the family tree unverified. each chart ends with a count: “15 of the 18 relationships shown are written in a record this archive has read. 3 come from the family tree and are unverified.” the nine pages with no chart say so in words, because a witness at a font with no recorded kin is a statement about the sources rather than about the person. twenty-eight households, sourced one at a time in site/src/data/kin.js. drawn in plain boxes and rules, deliberately not in svg — this archive once injected auto-links into an svg tree and silently erased half the names in it.
mijnwerker — an eighth child, and the last line of the testimony found

found four documents from the dutch reformed congregation at indwe, found by typing “indwe” into the register that was built yesterday. a willem hermanus booijzen, aged 21, is confirmed there on 31 may 1907, in a class that also holds catharina maria elizabeth roodt, 17, and susanna adriana roodt, 15. on 21 september 1908 he marries susanna adriana roodt, sixteen, at indwe — certificate 13, her parents consenting — and under rang of beroep the register writes mijnwerker, of dugmore mijn. two children are baptised at indwe, both entered onecht: willem hermanus, born 31 may 1908 to susanna adriana, and catharina willemina levina, born 8 february 1909 to catharina maria elizabeth — eight months and eight days apart, so the second name cannot be a slip for the first. at the first font, the third godparent is catharina maria sophia barry. this archive holds one woman of that name: kathleen, widowed at indwe in 1905. so the miner is her son, and this archive had no idea he existed.
withdrawn — “not one miner among them” taken back

found open question 10 said the mines claim was unsupported and that the occupations pointed away from it: saddler, farmer, mason, tree nurseryman, railway clerk, mason. “not one miner among them.” there is one, and the reason the archive missed him is worth stating plainly: the negative was built out of the occupations it happened to have read, and it had not read his because it did not know the man existed. a list of six is not a population. what replaces it is better than a simple yes — the boys did go onto the mines, and the first one this archive can name did it on cape coal at indwe in 1908, years before the family reached johannesburg and while his widowed mother was still living in the same town. the testimony compressed a slow migration into one train.

built from log.json and corrections.json at build time. if a finding is not here it is not in the log, and the build will say so before it says anything else — tools/drift.py fails the build when a narrative page and the data disagree. what was taken back →
what the retractions have in common
read them together and they fall into three kinds, and only one is about the records.

reading a document too eagerly. “armadale”, the two barry sisters, the z in an 1879 signature. in each case a faint or ambiguous mark was resolved in the direction that made the better story, and the correction came from looking harder or from a better scan.

not propagating a correction. “orphaned at seventeen” survived in four places after the date behind it had already been fixed. a correction is not finished when the fact changes; it is finished when everything that leaned on the fact changes.

reporting a search as wider than it was. the worst of them. the farm list negative was recorded before checking what the register held. a filtered search of the cape archives was written up as though it were the whole search, and twenty documents went unread — including james mountjoy's own wills. both were failures of description, not of luck, and both would have misled a later reader for years.
the distinction this archive keeps insisting on — “there is nothing there” against “nobody has looked” — is exactly the one it broke twice itself.

1905 · the death registration that settles the biggest question
cape colony, form of information of a death, act no. 7 of 1894. entry 299, sub-district indwe, district wodehouse. registered 14 september 1905.
death registration of willem hermanus booysen, indwe, 1905. myheritage tree defranceski family site (23andme), extracted 9 september 2026.
¦usual place of residence doorn street, indwe
¦age fifty five years
¦date of death september thirteenth 1905
¦intended place of burial public cemetery, indwe
¦cause of death ulcer of stomach
¦duration of last illness fourteen months
¦medical man w. c. macdonald, m.b.
¦informant j. b. booyzen — qualification: present at death
¦total children twelve
documented the death date the tree flagged "to be confirmed, not sure" is correct. he died at indwe on 13 september 1905.

documented he was not shot by the british. he died of a stomach ulcer after fourteen months of illness, under a doctor's care, in his own house, three years after the war ended. what that does to the testimony →
a farmer who became a mason
at his marriage in 1879 his occupation is boer — farmer. at his death in 1905 it is mason.

a man who works land and then works stone has, in between, very often lost the land. the war sits in that interval. inferred suggestive, not probative — but it is exactly the trajectory the burned-farm testimony describes.
the name changing, on one sheet of paper
the registering clerk writes the deceased's surname. four lines below, his son signs his own. they are not the same word.
the clerk, september 1905: willem hermanus booysen
his son, the same day: j. b. booyzen
the father is registered under the old spelling. the son signs the new one. both are on the same page, in september 1905 — three years after the anglo-boer war ended.

the informant is john barry booyzen (b. 1884), the eldest son, then twenty-one, recorded as present at the death. this is as close to a photograph of the surname changing as the archive is ever likely to find. the name →

marriage of willem hermanus booysen and catharine mary barry, barkly, 1879.
¦name as entered willem hermanus booysen catharine mary barry
¦status jongman jongedochter
¦rank or occupation boer (farmer) —

witnesses: j. sutherland and p. schoeman. set that beside anna johanna maria schoemann marrying hendrik nicholaas barry in 1877, the 1901 pretorius–barry wedding held at the home of d. schoeman, "caerlaverock", barkly east, and a commandant d. schoeman leading cape rebels at labuschagne's nek in 1900. the schoemans are braided through this family across three generations. the rebels →
the most consequential letter in the archive
the groom's own signature, 1879, at maximum available magnification.
the clerk wrote booysen. the groom signed what reads as "booij_en" — using the older dutch ij digraph, with a medial letter whose descending loop is more consistent with z than s.

if that reading is right, he was already signing with a z in 1879 — twenty years before the anglo-boer war — and the testimony's explanation of why the spelling changed is a later rationalisation of something that had already happened.

not established the reading is not certain. cursive dutch s and z are genuinely confusable, and this is a photograph of a duplicate register, not the original. the archive states both readings and prefers neither.

this single letter is now the most consequential unresolved question here. it wants an eye trained on nineteenth-century cape dutch hands, and the original register at the cape archives. open questions →

prepared by solicitors at barkly east, stamped 18 april 1915, no. 925. signed by james h. barry, "son (second)". this is the very document the family's earlier research note describes — it can now be quoted rather than paraphrased.
death notice of john barry, died 1903, notice prepared 1915.

¦father john barry (address unknown)
¦mother barry, born neagle (christian names and address unknown)
¦age 83 years (about)
¦occupation carpenter and builder
¦residence manorowen, barkly east district
¦spouse margaret wilhelmina elizabeth barry, born kolbe (died 2 august 1912). in community.

"at sea" is official, not folklore

the irish/high-seas ambiguity is contemporaneous and legal, sworn by his own son. the mother's maiden name neagle — almost certainly nagle, of county cork — is on a state document, not a family memory. the barrys →

the tree renders the farm "manor owen", which hides it. the notice types it as one word: manorowen — a village in pembrokeshire, wales. he also owned no immovable property: he lived on manorowen but did not own it. both are new and entirely unexplored.
two corrections fall out of this page.
1. the death date is 3 august 1903, not the 25 august the tree carries — a 22-day discrepancy.

2. a duplicate person is resolved. the tree lists both catherine maria sophia "kathleen" barry (1859–1940), married booyzen and a separate sister kathleen mary barry (booysen) with no dates. this notice lists only one barry daughter married to a boyson. the arithmetic closes exactly: the tree's 11 children = the notice's 8 surviving + 2 who predeceased him + 1 duplicate. they are the same woman, and the archive's earlier claim of "two barry sisters marrying booysens" is withdrawn.
1947 · george's death notice corrects his own death date
signed by g. booyzen at johannesburg on 21 february 1948 under the administration of estates act 1913.
death notice of george downing mountjoy booyzen, died 11 december 1947 at forest hill, johannesburg.
"the day of the decease: on 11th december 1947" — died at 85 rheeden st, forest hill, johannesburg.
he died on 11 december 1947 — not 21 february 1947.
21 february is the date the notice was signed, and it was signed in 1948. a transcriber conflated the two and lost ten months.

this also dissolves an anomaly this archive had itself flagged: a burial at west park recorded on 14 december 1947 looked like a ten-month delay. it was not. he died on the 11th and was buried on the 14th — three days later, exactly as one would expect.
age 46 years 6 months; occupation s.a.r. & h. — the south african railways and harbours; residence 85 rheeden street, forest hill.
surviving spouse gertruida alexandra booyzen, born kinnear, in community of property; pre-deceased spouse anna johanna maria booyzen (pretorius), died 26 february 1944.

children of the prior marriage. the two eldest are entered as majors; the four minors carry birth dates — 25/3/29, 12/10/30, 22/9/32, 10/1/34 — which match the tree exactly, independently confirming catherine mary sophia's birth on 25 march 1929. the second daughter is given a married name the tree does not have: kelly.
he worked for the railways, not the mines. the testimony's "the boys all got jobs on the mines" belongs to an earlier generation. by the 1940s this branch was s.a.r. & h. johannesburg →
the notice also records "no children of last marriage" — consistent with both infant gertrude elizabeths having died before him.

"george booyzen and isaak pretorius in transkei" — the tree's own caption. left: george downing mountjoy booyzen, in his thirties, in the wide trousers of the 1930s. right: isaak pretorius, a relative of george's wife, walking stick planted in the grass behind him. this appears to be the only photograph of george in the tree — his profile still carries myheritage's prompt to add a personal photo.
