attached to george's profile with no caption, no date and no tagging. the identifications below are inferred — reasoning is given so it can be overturned.

an elderly woman seated in full black between two young people, outside a plastered house. hypothesis: the seated woman is kathleen barry (1859–1940) in widow's black — the dress and print date the image to the 1930s, when she was in her seventies and living in johannesburg. unverified.
a young man in a dark uniform tunic and peaked cap. hypothesis: george downing mountjoy booyzen in south african railways and harbours uniform — the employer his 1947 death notice names. unverified.
a man in a light suit and fedora on a late-1920s sedan, registration tas 486, a small boy beside him. the registration is a hard, researchable detail. unidentified.
1819 · a sworn falsehood in shoreditch
a marriage allegation of the london diocese, 20 january 1819 — the sworn statement required before a marriage licence could be issued. fee, 2/6.
marriage allegation of george kolbe and margaret downing, london diocese, 20 january 1819, signed g. kolbe.

"appeared personally george kolbe and made oath, that he is of the parish of saint leonard shoreditch in the county of middlesex, a bachelor of the age of twenty-one years and upwards, and intendeth to marry with margaret downing of the same parish, a spinster of the age of twenty-one years and upwards…"
"…a bachelor of the age of twenty-one years and upwards."
both ages are false, and the document is an oath.
george augustus kolbe was born 7 december 1802. on 20 january 1819 he was sixteen years and six weeks old. margaret downing was born 23 february 1803; she was fifteen years and eleven months.

under hardwicke's marriage act of 1753 a minor under twenty-one could not marry by licence without a parent's consent. swearing to be "of the age of twenty-one years and upwards" was the ordinary way round it — and it was perjury. the four weeks' residence in the parish was very often nominal too.
this archive's 1820 settler married at sixteen, by lying under oath about his age, and sailed for africa eleven months later. the kolbes →
1844 · the estate the archive had a reference for but had never read
the cape archives reference kab mooc 6/9/35: 7698 (1845) was already noted here as "not yet ordered". it was in the family tree all along — the estate number 7698 is written at the head of the page.
death notice of george augustus kolbe, made under section 9, ordinance 104, at colesberg in january 1845 and signed m. kolbe — margaret, his widow.
the whole sheet, for anyone who wants to check the reading against it.
¦names of the parents left blank
¦condition in life agriculturist
¦day of the decease 1 december 1844
¦where died at knapdaar, in the field cornetcy of rhenosterberg, district of colesberg
¦property "about £1000 sterling"

the tree gives his occupations as reverend missionary of the london missionary society, chemist and tailor. the official record at the end of his life calls him simply an agriculturist, and he died on his own farm. those are not contradictions — they are a life in sequence — but the archive should stop leading with "missionary".
ten children, and one who is missing

the notice names ten. keetor peter benjamin kolbe, whom the tree gives a birth in 1840, is not among them — nor among the ten in his mother's 1867 notice. he died young, or he does not belong in this family. julia kolbe, whom myheritage flags as born two years after her father's death, is likewise absent, as she must be.

21 september 2026 — and “keetor” is not a name. a compiled register report of 2012 gives the same man as peter rector kolbe, which is a name, so the tree has been carrying a misreading. it matters because this archive holds anton rector kolbe barry (1882) and has never been able to say where his rector came from. a great-uncle of the name would say it. nothing is adopted — he is still in no document, and the same report splits him into two children, which is how it inflates its count. johan casimir, the fifth name on this notice, was in the same position until today: named here and again in 1867, and missing from this archive’s own people list. he now has a record.
1867 · margaret's death notice solves a problem this archive had raised
death notice of margaret downing, widow of the late george augustus kolbe, estate 4094, filed 30 january 1868 and signed by her son-in-law g. d. o. werdmuller.
¦names of the parents "both dead" — no names given
¦age 64 years 9 months & 2 days
¦day of the decease 25 november 1867
¦where died at her own residence in burghersdorp
¦property a dwelling house in burghersdorp and a farm in the division of albert; household furniture, live stock, sheep and cattle

"64 years 9 months & 2 days" on 25 november 1867 computes to a birth of 23 february 1803 — exactly what the tree says and exactly what the gravestone says. a three-way agreement, which in this archive is rare enough to be worth stating.

and it settles the enslin problem. this archive flagged an impossibility: margaretha kolbe appearing to marry george frederick enslin in 1850 while married to john augustus barry, and bearing enslin and barry children three and a half months apart in 1851. the archive's own guess was that the enslin children belonged to her sister mary elizabeth.

the notice lists, among margaret downing's children: "mary elizabeth (dead) who was married to george f. enslin — left issue of 6 minor children." resolved the enslin marriage and its children are mary elizabeth's, not margaretha's. the tree has attached one sister's family to the other. disputed →
one thing it does not give: her parents, entered only as "both dead". the tree's john paul downing and mary p king are therefore not corroborated here.
the grave at burgersdorp
the monument, inside its cast-iron enclosure, burgersdorp old cemetery.

sacred / to the memory of / george augustus kolbe, / born in london 7 december 1802, / and died at his farm wurthemburg, / division of albert, 1 december 1844. / also his relict / margaret downing, / born in london 23 february 1803, / and died at burghersdorp / 25 november 1867.

the farm is spelled wurthemburg in cut stone, with a th — closer to württemberg than the tree's "wurtemburg". and the stone says "his farm": he owned it, which margaret's 1867 notice confirms with "a farm in the division of albert".

she is commemorated under her maiden name, as his relict — the old word for widow. she outlived him by twenty-three years and was buried in his grave, as the dutch note on the myheritage record says: "zijn vrouw is later bijgezet in het graf."

the 1845 notice says district of colesberg; the stone says division of albert. both are right — albert, with its seat at burgersdorp, was carved out of the older district afterwards. the stone is the later text.
the portraits — and one that cannot be who it says
captioned "margaret elizabeth georgina downing and george kolbe" — and it is not them. see below.
margaret downing. heavily hand-retouched, but the centre parting and plain white collar fit the 1850s–60s, which fits a woman who died in 1867. plausible
george augustus kolbe. he died in 1844, when photography was five years old and vanishingly rare in the cape interior. if it is him, it is a copy of a painted miniature. unverified

the couple photograph is misattributed. it is a carte-de-visite — albumen print on a card mount with rounded corners. the woman wears a cuirass bodice with a long buttoned front, a ruched overskirt and a bustle; the man has a full beard and a watch chain. that costume is c. 1875–1885.
george augustus kolbe died in 1844. margaret downing died in 1867. neither can appear in a photograph taken in the late 1870s. a pencilled inscription on the mount does not appear to read "kolbe".

hypothesis it is their son george augustus kolbe (b. 1836) — who would be about forty in 1876, matching the sitter — with his wife. the repeated forename is the obvious route by which a caption goes astray. unproved.
st anne's, soho — where he was christened, 2 february 1803.
st leonard's, shoreditch — where he swore the oath and married, 20 january 1819.
1842 · the will of a bond street tailor
a prerogative court of canterbury register copy, from the public record office. signed 25 may 1842; proved at london 23 february 1846.
"this is the last will and testament of me john gottlob kolbe of conduit street, bond street, in the county…"

"…of middlesex tailor i give devise and bequeath all my estate both real and personal … unto timothy duke of lombard street, gentleman, christian william kent of bentinck street, poland street, tailor, and my daughter marian kolbe … upon trust."
the closing page and the probate act — proved at london, 23 february 1846, three months after his burial at the savoy.
he had a partner and a going concern

"…an agreement with my present partner mr richard davies that the executors … should permit the capital to be invested by me in our partnership business of tailors at the time of my death to remain in such business…" — for a term of fourteen years after he died.
this is not a jobbing tailor. it is a firm with capital, a partner, and a fourteen-year plan.
his daughter was an executrix
he appointed timothy duke, christian william kent and marian kolbe — his own daughter — "executors and executrix". at probate she is sworn as "marian kolbe spinster the daughter."
a woman administering a substantial estate in her own right in 1846 is worth pausing on.

and a provision with a sting in it. for those fourteen years the profits were to be divided among such of his daughters "as shall continue sole and unmarried" — and a daughter's share ceased entirely if she married, and was added to her unmarried sisters'. a maintenance fund for spinster daughters, and an incentive not to leave.

the residue: "…unto for and amongst all and every my child and children who may be living at the time of my decease in equal shares … and the issue of such of my children respectively as may be dead, such issue however to take only the share to which their parent would have been entitled."

george augustus kolbe died on 1 december 1844. his father died on 18 november 1845 — a year later. under that clause, george's share passed to his own children — to margaret downing's family at burgersdorp, and so to margaretha kolbe, who married john augustus barry.

inferred there is, on paper, a line of money from a bond street tailor's estate to the barkly east family. a later clause names "my said children or grandchildren" explicitly. whether a shilling of it ever reached the cape is unknown and untested — it would show in the pcc estate papers and in the cape estate files. open questions →

signed "j. g. kolbe", 25 may 1842, "written in one sheet of paper". witnessed by wm gribble jr and another, described as "clerks to mr duke, lombard street" — the executor's own clerks. proved at london the 23rd february 1846 before herbert thomas pratt, doctor of laws and surrogate.
1845 · two documents correct the tree twice over
general register office, entry 206, district of may fair within st george hanover square.
¦when died eighteenth of november 1845, at 34 conduit street
¦rank or profession tailor
¦cause of death "decay of nature" (certified) — the victorian phrase for old age

correction 1 — he did not die in lamb's conduit street
the tree records "34 lamb's conduit street". three independent documents say otherwise.
¦document address as given
¦death certificate, 1845 34 conduit street, registered at may fair
¦burial register, 1845 "conduit street, regent street"
¦his own will, 1842 "of conduit street, bond street, in the county of middlesex, tailor"

conduit street runs between regent street and new bond street, in mayfair. lamb's conduit street is in bloomsbury, over a mile away and in the holborn registration district — a death there could not have been registered at may fair.
the photograph in the tree captioned "34 lamb's conduit street" is a picture of the wrong building, in the wrong part of london. someone went and photographed a real 34 — just not his.
he lived and died above his own shop, in mayfair.
34 lamb's conduit street, bloomsbury — not the kolbe address.
correction 2 — he was not buried in warwickshire
the tree records "st john the baptist, leamington, warwickshire."
the register's own heading: "burials in the parish of st john baptist, in the german savoy church, in the county of middlesex."
entry no. 55: mr john gottlob kolbe, abode conduit street, regent street; died 18 nov, buried 26 november 1845, aged 81; ceremony by revd dr steinkopff, grave 7, rows 1–2.
the full page. entry 55 sits in a column of german names — which is rather the point of the correction.

somebody matched the dedication st john the baptist to the parish church at leamington spa. it is the german lutheran chapel royal of the savoy, in the strand — a hundred miles away, and the same congregation whose children's burial ground already holds five of his children and his wife mary larman.

the correction makes the family more coherent, not less. they are german lutherans of the savoy from first to last. the officiant, revd dr steinkopff, is karl friedrich adolf steinkopf (1773–1859), minister of the german savoy church and a founder of the british and foreign bible society. the kolbes →
the neighbouring entries in the register are almost all german — wüst, nitsch, wuleko, stürcke, kollmann, schnitzlein, grubusch, wettig. a german congregation in london, burying its own.
1901 · a wedding in a rebel's house, under martial law
the archive knew from a note in the tree that this marriage was held "at the home of d schoeman". the original register gives the man a signature.
marriage of petrus jacobus pretorius and magrita wilhelmina elizabeth barry, 8 july 1901. book 4584, entry 5. the card in the frame is the south african department of home affairs' damage notice.
¦occupation veeboer — stock farmer —
¦residence “arundale” (reading uncertain), barkly oost caerlaverock, barkly oost
"getrouwd in woonhuis d. schoeman te caerlaverock voormeld, na huwelijksgeboden, door mij: j. g. van der walt, pred. geref. kerk."
the witnesses: j. j. parsons and d. w. schoeman.

the initials are new, and they matter. in march 1900, about 400 cape rebels under commandant d. schoeman held labuschagne's nek, north of dordrecht — the next district over. sixteen months later a d. w. schoeman of caerlaverock, barkly east signs this register as a witness, in his own house, under martial law.
hypothesis that is now a specific, searchable identity to set against the rebel commandant lists — not the bare initial the archive had before. it is still not proof. the rebels →
married in a house, not a church

in the middle of the war, in a private dwelling. and in the gereformeerde kerk — the "dopper" church — not the nederduitse gereformeerde kerk in which willem hermanus booysen had married in 1879. a different, more conservative denomination.
and two more british farm names

he was of a farm whose name reads as “arundale” — the word is genuinely ambiguous at full magnification — and she of caerlaverock. set beside john barry's manorowen, the farms of this district carry scottish and welsh place-names — dumfriesshire, scotland, pembrokeshire.
inferred these are british settlers' farms, and the families on them were siding with the republics. that complicates the picture in a way worth keeping.

form of information of a death / aangifte van 'n sterfgeval, act no. 17 of 1923. entry 5970, district johannesburg.
¦name catherine mary sophia booyzen — "(born barry.)"
¦age · birthplace · condition 82 · cape province · widow

the two lines that place her at the end: no. 1, fifteenth avenue, mayfair, and brixton cemetery — a mile and a half apart, and both a long way from barkly east.
"8. occupation — home duties. 9. pensioner or dependent of pensioner — military pensioner."
an eighty-one-year-old widow in mayfair, drawing a military pension in 1940. her husband died in 1905 of a stomach ulcer, so it is not his service.

untested the likeliest route is a son's first world war service — several of her sons were of age — with a dependant's pension attaching to her. it is a hard, searchable fact and an entirely new thread in this archive.
it also carries an irony worth leaving in rather than smoothing away: a family that remembers fighting the british ends with its matriarch on a military pension in a british dominion.
two smaller gains. the archive had only "mayfair" for her death; it now has no. 1, fifteenth avenue. and the tree records no burial place for her at all — she is at brixton cemetery. johannesburg →
1912–1915 · "father: kolbe, thinks james was christian name"
of everything read in these four days, this is the line that most justifies the archive existing.

she died on 2 august 1912; her son completed the notice on 13 may 1915, nearly three years later. that gap matters — and it is the same gap as the 1840 montjoy notice, written thirteen years after that death, which answers the same question with "not known." in both cases the delay is part of the reason the answer is empty.
death notice for margaret elizabeth barry, born kolbe, who died 2 august 1912 in the house of her son at manorowen. signed r. p. barry, "son in whose house deceased died", barkly east, 13 may 1915.
"3. names and addresses of the parents of the deceased — father: kolbe, thinks james was christian name. mother: unknown."
her son, filling in his own mother's death notice, did not know his grandfather's name. he guessed james. of his grandmother he knew nothing at all.

his grandfather was george augustus kolbe — who married at sixteen on a sworn lie in shoreditch, sailed on the nautilus in 1819, preached across the orange river, named a karoo farm after his father's württemberg, and lies under a cut-stone monument at burgersdorp with his name, his london birth and his farm carved into it. his grandmother was margaret downing of london, buried in the same grave.
the family forgot them inside seventy years, while the headstone stood forty miles up the road.

resolved — by a better scan, and not in the direction expected

this section previously read the father's surname here as "booij_en", with the same ambiguous medial letter as the 1879 signature, and concluded: "i cannot separate them from an image… the change is real. its date is not established, and no scan will establish it."

that was read from a photograph of the register on the family tree. the archive has since read the cape town archives scan of the register itself, at nine times magnification. it is not ambiguous at all:
the father: petrus jacobus booyzen
the witnesses, same hand, same ink: pieterzen, twice

the letter is a z. and it is a z for the pieterzens too — a family with no name-change story attached to it. in dutch orthography -zen is simply how the patronymic ending is written, and this clerk wrote it that way for everyone.
the scan settled the letter. settling the letter is what took the argument away.

what this costs. the z cannot have been invented by anyone in this family — it was ordinary cape-dutch spelling, sitting in the registers in 1851. the 1879 signature question is not merely unsettled but largely emptied: a z-shaped letter in a dutch hand is not evidence of intent.

what survives, unchanged. the 1905 death registration, which turns on two spellings of one man's name on one sheet — clerk booysen, son booyzen — and not on the shape of any single letter. the tree's recorded "former name: booysen". and the distribution data: 646 against 53,764, gauteng against the cape, gathered a century later by people who had never heard of this family.
the change is real. the spelling it changed to was not new. the name →

the line reading "with consent of ————" is left empty. under hardwicke's act a minor marrying by licence needed a named consenting parent. the blank is the visible consequence of the oath they had sworn that morning: that both were "of the age of twenty-one years and upwards." he was sixteen; she was fifteen.

1840 · the oldest document in this archive — and it answers by refusing
kab mooc 6/9/21, reference 4393. named on the previous page as the most valuable unread document here. it has now been read.

how it was found. it is not name-indexed, and the probate collection's 846 films are catalogued by film number alone. the route was arithmetic: find any indexed 1840 death in the collection, take its film — 007844936, "cape province. probate records 1840–1843", 2,223 images — and read the reference numbers pencilled in the top corner of a handful of pages. they ascend by roughly one per image. image 700 is reference 4726; image 330 is 4386. interpolating and then narrowing put reference 4393 at image 339. it was there.

and this page said 338 for three weeks. corrected 9 october 2026, when all three frames were opened: 338 is the death notice of christoffel hendrik olivier, trader, dead at his own house in the town of graaff-reinet on 15 june 1840; 340 is willem jacobus van der merwe of bouwbosch fontein; montjoy is at 339, which is also where the familysearch record 1:1:qp4z-wk68 lands. the arithmetic above is why it was off, and it is worth keeping rather than tidying away. references do not ascend by exactly one per image — an estate running to two or three frames breaks the step — so from image 330 at 4386 the method predicts 4393 at image 337, and the narrowing that followed stopped one frame short of the right page. an interpolated citation is a prediction, and it has to be re-read off the frame it actually landed on. nothing in the reading below changed: every line of it is confirmed.

generation seven of this family has stood at the head of the direct line since this archive began with the flattest entry on the site: no birth date, no death date, no father, no mother. he was there because the family tree said so, and for no other reason. everything below him had documents. he had a name.

he now has a document too. not his own — his son's. in september 1876, at a farm in the transvaal, somebody was asked who the dead man's parents were and wrote down gerthardus lödewikus booijsen and magdalena de beer.

it does not date him, and it does not name his parents, so the oldest open question on this site stays open. what it does is move the two of them out of the tree and into the record, and that matters more than it sounds, because this archive had already found a reason to distrust the pairing. searching the cape depot for magdalena de beer's estate turned up kab ncd 2/1: 49, a notarial will of 1793 for "jan booysen, married to the late magdalena de beer" — a different husband, and a wife fifty years too early. it was recorded as a warning that booysen–de beer was not a unique pairing.
it still is not. but the pairing in this line is no longer an assertion, and the 1793 will can now be set aside for good rather than merely resisted.

a man who had not seen this document predicted what is on it, in thirteen minutes. on 14 september 2026 pieter van zyl answered the g2g question about this document. he had not seen this page. he wrote: "his real dad, jan, was already dead for more than 40 years when petrus jacobus died… quite possibly, the informant 'thought' the dad's name was g l. i searched for a marriage between a gerhardus lodewicus and magdalena de beer but could not find one. if i remember correctly, there was a child of petrus called gerhardus lodewicus on his sterfkennis."

there is. he is in the table above. the fifth child in line 12 is jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen — and the name this archive takes from line 3, for the dead man's father, is the back half of his son's name. both are on the same sheet of paper, eight lines apart, in one clerk's hand.

de villiers puts petrus jacobus under jan (b3c4d7). the son on this page is jan gerthardus lodewikus. the informant had a compound name in the house and wrote half of it into the wrong line, dropping the half that agreed with the printed genealogy. that is a mechanism, not a guess, and it is visible without leaving the document.

what this does and does not do. it does not prove the father was jan; this archive is not swapping one unproved father for another on the strength of a good reading. what it does is remove this document as decisive evidence for gerthardus lodewikus — which is a real loss, because line 3 is the only place that name has ever been found. the question stays open and gets harder. disputed →

and this changes the map. this archive has spent its life treating the family as a cape family that went north to johannesburg in the twentieth century, and treating the booyzens of the western transvaal as strangers who happened to share a surname. the direct ancestor died in district rustenburg in 1876 — twenty-five years before the war, a generation before johannesburg. two other notices read the same afternoon sit in the same country: a magdalena susanna maria van den berg, born booyzen, who died at vaalbank in the district of lichtenburg in 1920 and whose father is entered as jan gerhardus lodewicus booyzen; and an an anna johanna booijzen, born in the district of cradock about 1823, who died on a farm in the district of rustenburg in 1891, leaving children called petrus jacobus, magdalena johanna and hendrik stephanus nicolaas. neither was proved to be kin when this was written. both are the right names in the right district at the right time, and this archive could no longer say what it had been saying. what was withdrawn →

1902 · a wrong name in the index, and a right family behind it
searching the cape probate index for hercules johannes mountjoy returns exactly one hit. it is not his.
kennisgeving van sterfgeval, filed 3 january 1903. carolina deybella margrietta alletta van niekerk, geboren botha, died at her own house at dordrecht, 18 december 1902.
because his name is written on it. fifth in her list of eleven children:
"5. maria sophia van niekerk, getrouwd met hercules johannes mountjoy."

the familysearch index keys every name on the page, so a search hit is not a statement about whose document it is. hercules johannes still has no estate file, and this archive's finding on that stands. what has changed is that the one false positive has been opened and turns out to be his mother-in-law.

so the van niekerks are now documented. maria sophia van niekerk, who married hercules johannes mountjoy at dordrecht on 8 october 1888, was a daughter of jan dirk abram frans van niekerk and carolina deybella margrietta alletta botha, who was herself born in the district of cradock and whose parents were philip rudolph botha and a mother of the same long name.

her ten brothers and sisters were carolina deybella margrietta alletta, cornelius, maria francina cecilia (widow of gert olivier), jan dirk abram frans, hercules johannes, christiaan jacobus, cornelia elizabeth gertruida (married james ross), benjamin jacobus, pieter jacobus and philip rudolph.

she had a brother called hercules johannes, and she married a man called hercules johannes. this archive notes that and does nothing with it. it is the kind of coincidence that invites a story, and there is no document behind any story it invites.
the notice is signed by her widower, j. d. a. f. van niekerk, and it is one more piece of evidence that dordrecht is where this side of the family married. dordrecht →

the last line of the family testimony reads: "after the war our great great grandmother put herself and her kids on a train to johannesburg where the boys initially all got jobs on the mines to make ends meet." this archive tested it, found six occupations across five generations — saddler, farmer, mason, tree nurseryman, railway clerk, mason — and wrote, on the open questions page: "not one miner among them."

but read what it actually says, because the detail is wrong in a way that matters. indwe is a colliery town in the north-eastern cape — coal, not gold — and this is 1908. the testimony puts the mines after a train to johannesburg. the family was still at indwe. so the claim is now supported and mislocated at the same time: the boys did go onto the mines, and the first one to do it did it three hundred miles from johannesburg and years before the family got there. indwe →

the archive holds exactly one catharina maria sophia barry: kathleen, born 1859, married to willem hermanus booyzen in 1879, widowed at indwe in september 1905. dutch reformed registers enter women under their maiden names, and there she is, in december 1908, standing godmother.

inferred the miner is her son. no document says so in words. what the documents say is that a willem hermanus booyzen born about 1886 was living at indwe, and that kathleen barry stood at his child's font. this archive is satisfied and says which of those two things is the evidence.

the remark column is the harder reading. onecht — born out of wedlock. the child was born on 31 may 1908; the parents married on 21 september 1908; the baptism was on 6 december. the register records the child's status at birth and does not revise it.

it also fixes where the family was. kathleen barry was still at indwe in december 1908, three years and three months after her husband died there. whatever else the train to johannesburg was, it was not immediate.

1885 · the estate this archive gave to the wrong man
no image, no transcription, no new document read. just an index line, set against two that have been read — and a correction that moves a whole branch of this family onto the map.

since the transvaal references were first pulled out of naairs, this archive has carried a row saying tab mhg o/2899 — jan gerhardus lodewikus booyzen — 1885, and attached it to the seventh child on the 1863 death notice: jan gerhardus lodewicus booysen, born 4 december 1855. his entry on the people index read "he died in the transvaal at about thirty."

he did not. that sentence had no source except the estate reference itself. the archive read the year off the file number, wrote it into his life as a death date, and then quoted the death date back as if it were evidence.

jan gerhardus lodewicus booysen, born 4 december 1855, no longer dies in 1885. this archive does not know what became of him, and now says so. he was seven when his mother died and twenty-nine when his father's estate was wound up, and after that there is nothing.
one more name back in the queue at open questions.
second, a farm joins the line

the uncle died at vaalbank, district lichtenburg. this archive has already read a sterfkennis from that farm: magdalena susanna maria van den berg, born booyzen, died there on 1 may 1920, aged 59 years 9 months, father entered as jan gerhardus lodewicus booyzen.
she was recorded here as a lead that was "not proved". she is his daughter, born about 1860, on a farm where her father had died thirty-five years before.

this is the third time the western transvaal has moved closer. first the 1876 sterfkennis put the direct ancestor in district rustenburg in 1876, which cost this archive its flat claim that the marico booyzens "are not this family". now his son is at vaalbank in the district of lichtenburg — the next district west — and his granddaughter is still on the same farm in 1920. marico is the third district in that row. it still is not proved, and the atlas still says unresolved. but the distance keeps shrinking, and it has only ever shrunk in one direction. the atlas →

here is a woman named booyzen, born about march 1754, who died in 1843, whose estate sits in the cape master's papers — and whose name is not magdelena, not elisabeth, and not de beer. she was the widow of a du plessis and she died in a rented house in cape town.

this archive does not say they are the same person. it says the opposite. but a birth year and a death year matching to the year, on the only two facts the tree offers, is exactly the material a records-matcher builds a wrong person out of — and it is worth knowing that such a record exists before somebody finds it and decides it is her. open question zero →

one thing she does show, and it is not nothing. booyzen was a cape surname before this family's paper trail starts. she was born in the colony in 1754, which is a year earlier than anything else in this archive, and she died owning fifteen pounds of somebody else's debt.

the 1908 death notice names four children — petrus jacobus (deceased), ockert johannes stephanus, anna catharina grobelaar and aletta catharina johanna venter — and does not say which wife they belong to. this archive drew all four under the second wife, charlotta, because she was the marriage it could name.

they cannot be hers. she married him on 14 april 1892 at the age of fifty-one, a widow. by 1908 two of the four are married women carrying their husbands' surnames, one is dead, and the fourth signs his father's death notice as an adult son. every one of them was born long before 1892. the four children belong to the first wife, anna catharina johanna olivier, and the household that has stood empty on this site since the 1908 notice was read is the one they go in. the households → · what was taken back →

brakfontein is not a strange farm. it is the farm. sterfkennis no. 678 for petrus jacobus booijsen, the oldest document on this site, was written at brakfontein on 14 september 1876 and signed there by his son hendrik stefanus. sixteen years after that, the zeerust register gives hendrik stefanus's home as brakfontein, rustenburg. a woman dying on that farm in 1891 was never a stranger. one letter — a k read for an r — kept her off this family for a week.
line one, enlarged three times. "gebooren oliefier."

the letters are o · l · i · e · f · i · e · r. there is no b, no r-t-s, and no second syllable that could carry -berts. oliefier is how a man who writes booijzen, stefanes and brakfontijn spells olivier.

and the archive does not have to guess, because her own son wrote her name down again. seventeen years later, filling in his father's death notice, ockert johannes stephanus booysen gave the first wife as "anna catharina johanna booysen, born olivier". the 1908 notice →

"ongehuwd" · "14 mei 1891" · "op de plaas brakfontijn, destrict rustenburg." the same farm as his mother's, five days on.
line three, enlarged. "hendrick stefanes booijsen en anna catrena gebooren oliefier." the same word, in the same hand, on the second notice.

a twenty-nine-year-old farmer, unmarried, with nothing but movables worth under twenty-five pounds, dead on his father's farm five days after his mother. the archive cannot say what killed either of them and the notices do not ask. what it can say is that brakfontein lost two people in one week in may 1891, and that the man left standing was a widower of sixty-two with six grown children — who married again, at zeerust, eleven months later.

this is what the archive gets back. a wife with a name, her parents, her birth district and her seven children; a son nobody knew existed; a farm confirmed as the family's own; and the origin of a forename that had no business being there. all of it came out of a page this site had already found, already filed, and read wrongly twice.

the first row is the one that matters. a baptism register at rustenburg, indexed by somebody who never saw this site, gives the parents of a boy born 31 january 1862 as hendrik stephanus booijsen and anna johanna olivier.

31 january 1862 is not a date this archive had. it is a date it calculated, an hour earlier, by subtracting 29 jaar 3 maanden en 14 dagen from 14 mei 1891 on a torn death notice. the two agree to the day. and the register spells the mother's name in full, in a hand a volunteer could read, thirty years before the death notice this archive misread as alberts. the 1891 notices →
two brothers, one sunday

on 3 april 1869 two sons of the house were admitted to membership at rustenburg together: petrus jacobus, born 20 april 1851, and ockert johannes stephanus, born 15 september 1852. they are the first and second names on their mother's 1891 list, seventeen and sixteen at the time, and they are the two who appear again on their father's 1908 notice — one of them dead by then, the other signing it.

ockert died at klerksdorp on 16 january 1921, aged sixty-nine. that is a civil registration and it names no parents, which is the whole difficulty with civil death records in this country and the reason this archive keeps going back to sterfkennisse.
where a name goes once it is in

ocken johannes oliefier, of the district of cradock, had a grandson called ockert johannes stephanus booysen — who had a nephew called ockert johannes stefanus, baptised at rustenburg in 1894. three generations of a forename that came into this family with one marriage, and this archive could not account for any of them a day ago.

the other direction runs the same way. hendrik stephanus nicolaas booyen was born on 4 january 1882 and named for his uncle — who was twenty at the time and would be dead on his father's farm before the boy was ten. the nephew lived until 8 october 1959, at kempton park, and outlived the man he was named for by sixty-eight years. the namesakes →

1908 & 1932 · the second willem hermanus — married at sixteen and twenty-two, dead in booysens

this archive has had willem hermanus booyzen of indwe as a name with a beginning and no end: a lidmaat at indwe in 1907, a mijnwerker on two baptisms, a marriage known only from an index, and then nothing at all after 1910. two things are new here. the marriage register page itself has now been read, and it is worth reading. and the end of him has been found: he died in a johannesburg hospital on 29 july 1932, an ex-miner, and was buried at brixton two days later.

married. since 1908.
forty-seven in july 1932 against twenty-two in september 1908 — which makes him forty-six. one year.

brixton cemetery, 31 july 1932, where the burial register gives his birth as 1885 and where this family already buries its johannesburg dead: anna j. mary booyzen in 1914, john barry booyzen in 1916, george downing daschner in 1925.
and “sasanna adriana booyzen” was buried at johannesburg in 1968 — his widow, under his name, thirty-six years after him.

no parents are named, because a south african civil death registration does not ask for them unless the deceased is under ten. that is the whole reason this archive keeps going back to sterfkennisse, and it is why this identification is marked inferred and not documented.
familysearch indexes his age as 44. the form says 47. read the image, not the index — a lesson this site learned twice today.
the occupation itself was “told” to the clerk, by a hospital official who wrote the word in brackets. nobody who knew him was in the room.
grave 6889 — and the identification closes
town council of johannesburg · consecutive grave numbers. grave 6889: boysen, william — folio 49; and beneath him susanna adriana booyzen · 29.8.68.

they are in the same grave. everything above is circumstantial — the occupation, the province, the age, the cemetery. this is not. the johannesburg grave register puts william booyzen and susanna adriana booyzen in grave 6889, thirty-six years apart, and susanna adriana roodt is the woman he married at indwe on 21 september 1908.

note how the clerk spells him: boysen. that is the same spelling an english clerk put on john barry’s 1915 death notice — “kathleen mary boyson, born barry, married in community of property to william boyson” — for a different man of the same family, seventeen years earlier and eight hundred kilometres away. the name →

his father died of a stomach ulcer at indwe in 1905, aged fifty-four. this man died of a perforated duodenal ulcer at johannesburg in 1932, aged forty-seven. twenty-seven years and eight hundred kilometres apart, and the same organ.

he left the coal at indwe for the gold on the rand, as the whole family did, and he was living at 62 langford street in booysens — a johannesburg suburb that has nothing to do with this family and is spelled like it. he was in hospital about a day. the man who reported his death was the hospital's own officer. the atlas → · open questions →

that is the seventh death notice in this archive that fails to name a parent. a husband of ten years knew his wife’s father’s name and not her mother’s. it is the same failure as james montjoy in 1840, as john barry’s son in 1915 writing neagle and admitting he had neither her christian names nor an address, and as the 1876 sterfkennis that names eight children and no mother for any of them.

yesterday anna catharina johanna olivier did not exist on this site. this morning she was recovered from a death notice the archive had misread twice. this afternoon there are two more documents: her baptism at cradock in 1824 and her marriage at potchefstroom in 1850 — and the second of them moves the whole family’s history twenty-six years.

and she had a sister baptised at cradock eleven months earlier: aletta catharina olivier, 4 october 1823, same parents. anna johanna’s own daughter is aletta catharina johanna. the names in this family go back up the female line and this archive could not see it until today. the namesakes →

entries 189 to 207, june and july 1850. three columns only: namen der gehuwden, ouderdom, wanneer gehuwd. no parents, no birthplaces, no occupations — a frontier register keeping the minimum.
entry 206. namen der gehuwden · ouderdom · wanneer gehuwd. hendrik stephanus booijzen, 23 · anna johanna olivier, 25 — the date carried down by ditto marks from 3 july 1850.
her name, written plainly, forty-one years early

the 1891 death notice spells her maiden name oliefier in a hand so bad this archive read it as alberts and threw her out of the family for a week. here it is in 1850, in a clerk who could write: olivier. four documents now agree — 1850 potchefstroom, 1862 rustenburg, 1891 brakfontein, 1908 koedoesfontein. how it was misread →

he was 23 in july 1850, so born about 1827 — against about june 1828 from the 1908 notice and 63 at zeerust in 1892. she was 25, so born about 1825 — against a baptism of 10 september 1824. four independent estimates, all inside two years. their eldest son petrus jacobus was born on 20 april 1851, nine and a half months after the wedding.
the date that matters most is the place.

this archive has spent its whole life pushing back the moment this family crossed into the transvaal. it began by saying they went north to johannesburg by railway in the twentieth century. then the 1876 sterfkennis put the direct ancestor dead in the district of rustenburg — twenty-five years before the war, a generation before johannesburg — and that was already the earliest evidence there was.

they were married at potchefstroom on 3 july 1850. that is twenty-six years earlier again, fourteen years after the great trek, and two years before the sand river convention made the south african republic a state at all. a booijzen was standing in a transvaal church before there was a transvaal. the atlas →

the disputed page has carried this since the first week:

“the tree marries her to petrus jacobus booysen in 1805 at graaff-reinet and has her dead before march 1825. familysearch carries a dutch reformed marriage of petrus jacobus booÿzen and anna maria van der merwe dated 9 march 1825, at cape town, indexed three separate times. either the death date was derived from this very record by someone reading it as an end rather than a beginning, or the 1825 marriage is a different couple entirely. the archive is not going to guess which.”

this archive lost the direct ancestor’s brother in march 1904, signing his wife’s death notice at pretoria. here he is nineteen months later, in the same city, marrying again — and the remarks column does something this archive has never seen a marriage register do.

entry 105 (rm 524), duplicate original register, marriage solemnized at pretoria. eleven columns, and the last one is what matters.

“remarriage certificate from master supreme court no. 4795, dated 4/11/05.”
4795 is the number of his first wife’s death notice.

it is the document read on this same page a few sections up: the notice for elizabetha margaretha booijzen, born marais, who died in a zinc building in market street on 1 june 1900 and whose file he did not open until march 1904. the master would not let a widower remarry until the first estate was in order, so he issued a certificate out of that file on 4 november 1905 — and the marriage clerk copied the estate number into the register three weeks later.

this is not an inference. it is a reference number written on one document pointing at another. the david schalk booyzen who married at pretoria in 1905 is the david schalk booijzen who was widowed there in 1900, and both of them are the david schalk booysen born 9 june 1848 — fourth on the 1863 list, the direct ancestor’s brother.

and the birthplace is cradock. his mother johanna catharina mountjoy was married at cradock in november 1838; his first wife was born in the district of cradock about april 1850; and his brother willem hermanus was born achter sneeuberg three years after him. the family was moving around one corner of the karoo and this is the first document to say where he started.

a method worth keeping. the remarks column of a transvaal civil marriage register carries the master’s estate number whenever a widow or widower remarries. that is a direct index from a marriage to an estate file — and it works in the direction this archive usually cannot go, from a person who is alive to a file about somebody who is dead.
what is still missing: his own death. he was alive and fifty-six in november 1905, at goede hoop in pretoria, and this archive still cannot find the end of him. what is still to ask →

a hawker of goedehoop with twelve children, six of them still minors, who died on 5 june 1905 in the pretoria asylum. his widow signed the notice on 27 october and married david schalk booyzen one month later, on 27 november. the master cleared her remarriage certificate on the 7th of that month and david schalk’s on the 4th.

between the two certificates stand twenty children — eight booijzens and twelve lowieses, six of the lowieses under age. that is what the remarks column of a marriage register is protecting, and it is why the master would not let either of them marry until the estates were settled.

and then october 1918
richard peter booyzen, twenty-four years old, buried at brixton on 27 october 1918.
that is the exact centre of what johannesburg called black october — the second wave of the influenza, which killed something like fourteen thousand people on the rand in six weeks.

this archive does not have a richard peter booyzen. it should. richard peter barry is kathleen barry’s brother, named on their father’s 1903 registration and on the cape rebel roll; and a boy born about 1894 falls exactly in the gap in willem hermanus and kathleen’s children, between catharina maria sophia in 1891 and george downing mountjoy in 1901. a booyzen child named after his mother’s brother, buried in the cemetery where this family buries. inferred, and added as a ninth child with the reasoning on his page — a burial register names no parents and this one is no exception.

he is not alone in that register. john zacharia booysen, twenty-nine, was buried at brixton on 26 november 1918, and johanna a. booysen, nought days old, on 19 december 1918. this archive cannot show that either is kin — there is no forename in this family that reaches them, and booysen is a common name on the rand. they are set down here because the shape is the point: three booysens into one cemetery in eight weeks, in the worst two months south africa has had.
