a fourth booyzen stone in the same ground, and no connection to the other three that this archive can find. the cape civil register carries her under a chain of surnames that is its own biography — booyzen byleveld langenbog booyzen — and dates her birth 1857 where the stone says 1855. her probate names her husband johannes hendrik. she died twelve weeks before pieter j. went into the same cemetery. same surname, same town, same year: exactly the shape that gets two families welded into one, which is why she is written down here and not quietly left out.

what four stones in one cemetery are worth. between them they moved a birth from a guessed month to a date, a death from a year to a month, and confirmed two dates this archive already had from sources that had nothing to do with the ones it got them from. none of that is a new person. it is the difference between a record and a corroborated record, and it took one search and five photographs.
1940 · the pillar at silverton — twelve household names, matched to eleven legal ones

the centre pillar of the double stone at silverton lists the children of stefanus francois booyzen and beatrix magdalena catharina boshoff by the names they were called at home. his 1940 estate lists eleven children by the names they were registered under. the two lists have never been set side by side, and doing it identifies a twelfth child.
¦on the stone on the 1940 estate how the match is made
¦ouboet david schalk booyzen not a name: ouboet is afrikaans for eldest brother. matched by position — he heads the estate list.
¦ousie susanna fredrika aletta booyzen not a name either: ousie, eldest sister. matched by position — and she is the only daughter left over once the other three are matched by name.
¦bessie elizabeth magrieta booyzen bessie ← elizabeth
¦betie beatrix magdalena catharina booyzen betie ← beatrix — her mother's name entire
¦henna johanna catharina booyzen henna ← johanna. the weakest of the nine: henna can also stand for hendrina, and there is no hendrina on the estate.
¦evert ewert philippus booyzen the same name, spelt as the family said it
¦✝ baba nobody a twelfth child. cut with a birth star and a cross and no name at all — baba is simply baby. not on the 1940 estate because the child was already dead when it was written.
¦fanie stephanus francois booyzen the younger fanie ← stefanus. standard, and unambiguous.
¦willie willem hendrik booyzen willie ← willem
¦pietie petrus jacobus booyzen pietie ← petrus
¦johan johan abraham frederik booyzen the same name
¦hennie hendrik rudolph philippus booyzen hennie ← hendrik

eleven names on the estate, twelve on the stone, and every one of the eleven is claimed exactly once. that is what makes the twelfth real. nine of the matches are ordinary afrikaans diminutives; two — ouboet and ousie — are not names but places in the family, and they fall to the two children the diminutives leave over. nothing is left unassigned except ✝ baba.

this archive has met this shape before. joseph heinrich daschner's 1942 death notice named eleven children; the brixton burial register turned up a twelfth, george downing daschner, three months and five days old, buried in 1925 and therefore not on a notice written seventeen years later. the register → a death notice lists the living. a gravestone, cut by the family, lists the children. that is the difference between the two documents, and it is worth more than either of them alone.

what is not claimed. no birth date, no sex, no order of birth beyond the stone's own order, and no name — the child is entered here as baba booyzen because that is the only word cut for it. the matches above are readings of nicknames, not documents, and the household page marks every one of them as inferred rather than stated. the mother's own name is on the stone as betie's: the family reused it inside one generation.
what was searched today and not found

four questions worked properly and answered no, or not yet. they are set down at the same length as the finds, because a family history that publishes only its successes is asking to be believed on trust.
elizabetha van der merwe’s marriage

the second wife of petrus jacobus booysen (1788–1876), named on her son’s 1908 death notice. if the marriage could be dated it would split the eight children of the 1876 sterfkennis between two mothers instead of leaving all eight under a printed warning. searched: booysen × van der merwe marriages across all south african collections; elizabeth van der merwe with a booysen spouse; the cape registers 1820–1835. nothing. every booysen–van der merwe marriage the indexes carry is twentieth century. the eight stay under the warning.
the four remaining 1876 children

david schalk, magdalena johanna, anna eliezabet, eliezabet cornelia and anna maria booijsen — five of the eight on the 1876 sterfkennis with no document of their own. still none. the transvaal probate index carries nobody of those names who can be tied to this family, and the cape index carries too many. the three that were settled today — petrus jacobus, jan gerthardus lodewikus and hendrik stefanus — were all settled by somebody else’s death notice, not their own.
ockert johannes stephanus booysen’s estate

he died at klerksdorp on 16 january 1921 and has no estate file of his own in the indexed transvaal probate records. six index hits under four spellings, every one of them him as somebody else’s relative. his death is a civil registration, which names no parents, and the films are not ordered by estate number so there is nothing to browse along. what was found instead →
the three untraced daughters

anna johanna maria, elesabettha maria cornelya and magdalena johanna booijsen, all of age on their mother’s 1891 notice and on nothing else. two of the three are probably dead before 1908, because their father’s notice names four children where their mother’s named seven. and this archive cannot show that the anna catharina grobelaar of 1908 is the anna johanna maria of 1891: the forenames do not agree, and guessing that they do is the exact mistake this site spent today undoing.
two questions worked hard and not closed

both of these were predicted to fail before they were started. one did. the other moved further than expected, and neither is resolved — which is set out here at the same length as the finds, because that is the only way the finds are worth anything.
1 · whose son was stephanus francois booyzen?

he sits on this site as a son of petrus jacobus booysen and his second wife johanna margaritha pretorius, placed there on his birth date alone because his own 1940 sterfkennis names neither parent — his widow wrote oorlede for both. then the 1900 death notice of elizabetha margaretha marais named a stephanus françois booijzen as a son of david schalk booijzen, and the dispute opened.
duplicaat origineel register · huwelijk bevestigd te mosselbaai. eight columns — and none of them asks where anybody was born, which is the whole difficulty.
entry 1318, duplicaat origineel register, mosselbaai, 5 september 1905.
what the register gives

stefanus francois booyzen, 30, jonkman — a bachelor — metselaar, a mason, woonplaats tijdens het huwelijk: pretoria. he married beatrix magdalena catharina boshoff, 16, jongdochter of mosselbaai, with her ouders consenting, in the n.g. kerk by john murray.
what it does not give

no parents. no birthplace. this register has a column for woonplaats tijdens het huwelijk and none for waar geboren — unlike the zeerust register of 1892, which gave this archive hendrik stefanus’s graaff-reinet. the question is not settled and this document cannot settle it.

but it tilts. in september 1905 stephanus francois was a bachelor of thirty living at pretoria. the 1900 notice calls david schalk’s son stephanus françois an unmarried major; and eleven weeks later, on 27 november 1905, david schalk booijzen of goede hoop, pretoria married again in that same city.

two booyzens in pretoria in one autumn, one of them exactly the bachelor son the 1900 notice describes. against that: the existing placement rests on a birth year and nothing else, and both men are masons, which discriminates nothing — willem hermanus was a mason at indwe too, and he is either this man’s half-brother or his uncle depending on which reading wins.
still marked serious. it moves, it does not close, and this archive is not going to decide a father on a city. disputed →
2 · the oliviers of cradock

anna catharina johanna olivier’s parents came into this archive yesterday as two names on a baptism. the problem stated then was that at least four men of nearly that name were baptising children in that church in the 1820s, and separating them is the only way her line goes higher. they are not separated. but this couple now has a footprint of its own.
¦8 dec 1816 they marry graaff-reinet — index only, no image
¦25 jul 1820 gert cornelis olivier born baptised 2 oct 1820, cradock
¦15 may 1823 aletta catharina olivier born baptised 20 oct 1823, cradock

they married at graaff-reinet. that is the town where petrus jacobus booysen was baptised in 1788, where his son was born in 1812, where jan gerardus lodewicus was born in 1818 and where hendrik stefanus was born about 1829. the oliviers and the booysens were in the same small karoo town at the same time, moved to cradock, and their children married each other at potchefstroom in 1850, six hundred miles north.

what is still not done: four children is not a family, an index entry with no image is not a marriage register, and this archive still cannot tell this ockert johannes stephanus olivier from the ockert johannis fredrik lodewyk, the okker petrus jacobus and the ockert johannes frederik who were all baptising at cradock in the same decade. her line still stops with her parents.

one more thing worth noticing. the form asks where the marriage took place and the answer is "burghersdorp (probably)". a son of the house, writing twelve years after his father's death and three after his mother's, does not know where his parents were married and says so in brackets. it sits beside line 3, where he gives his grandmother's surname as neagle and admits he has neither her christian names nor an address.

this is the same failure this archive has been tracking since 1840, in a family that wrote in english and filed with a solicitor. six death notices here fail to name a parent properly; two of them are john barry's and his wife's.

and where the commandant’s farm turned out to be, two hours from bloemfontein, when the fauresmith pin was withdrawn earlier this month.

two of those three places are this family’s own ground, and one is the vaalbank whose farm school this archive documented a week ago. it is a lead and not a finding. this archive has already shown that david schalk is a van der merwe name before it is a booysen one, and there are fifty-four booysens and twenty booyens in the same list. a petrus jacobus booysen, aged 27, of pretoria and pietersberg, is among them — the right name, the wrong generation, and recorded here so that he is not later mistaken for the petrus jacobus this archive holds.

1841 and 1851 · the yorkshire john barry is real, and he is a shipowner at whitby

open question 6 has stood since it was written: one profile welds a yorkshire farmer of bilsdale, christened 1796 and buried at st hilda’s on 3 january 1853, to a john barry who died at de bruins poort in the cape on 8 january 1853, five days later. the burial registers have already been searched and hold no barry at bilsdale at all. the censuses do better than a negative: they produce the man.
1841 · ho107/1265, book 11, folio 38, page 4
john barry, head, aged 45, born yorkshire. address ship yard, ruswarp, whitby. schedule 1116. in the house with him: jno, mary, ann and catharine barry.
1851 · ho107/2374, folio 563, page 12, line 6
john barry, head, married, aged 55, born whitby. occupation ship owner. address ship yards, ruswarp, whitby. schedule 46. with mary (b. 1809), catherine (b. 1832) and elizabeth (b. 1836).

he is not a farmer, he is not of bilsdale, and he is alive in 1851. ruswarp is a township on the esk a mile above whitby harbour, thirty miles from bilsdale across the moor. the occupation is ship owner and the street is ship yards.
and there is nobody else he could be

not one of the hundred and two is in the helmsley registration district, which is the district bilsdale sits in. and across both censuses there is exactly one john barry born in 1796 in the whole north riding: the shipowner at ruswarp, in 1841 at ship yard and in 1851 at ship yards, the same house ten years apart.
what question 6 becomes

the english half of that profile has been taken apart and rebuilt. there is a real john barry born in the north riding in 1796. he is a whitby shipowner, not a bilsdale farmer of holly bower; there is no barry in 5,934 indexed bilsdale burials; and he was still keeping house at ruswarp in the spring of 1851. whether he is the man the tree meant or a man the tree found and dressed in somebody else’s clothes, he cannot also have been buried at st hilda’s.

what is still open, and it is a smaller question than it was: whether the whitby shipowner has any connection at all to the john barry who died at de bruins poort. nothing here says he does. the five-day coincidence that built the profile is now a coincidence with nothing on the english side of it.

and the move that the rate books could only bracket

the westminster rate books have him in church street south to 1831. the gazette has him in conduit street by september 1836. between those two dates the family left soho for mayfair, and he was working with a partner at each end — david fletcher to 1836, richard davies to march 1845.
which makes the obituary’s “esq. of brunswick-square” harder still. he was signing himself a tailor in the gazette eight months before he died.

all five are free. the london gazette’s own archive at thegazette.co.uk is searchable back to 1665 and returns the ocr text in an atom feed — /all-notices/notice/data.feed?text=… with a publication-date range. this archive found the 1836 notice months ago and never ran the same search again with the dates widened. the other four had been sitting there the whole time.
9 january 1819 · a brother of the settler says where his father lives

this archive spent a fortnight arguing about a london address from obituaries, wills and tax books. the son of the house answered it out loud, in a courtroom, in january 1819, and somebody wrote it down.
the proceedings of the old bailey · session of 13 january 1819 · trial t18190113-149
309. richard kerr was indicted for stealing, on the 9th of january, one coat, value 6l., the property of john henry kolbe.

john henry kolbe. my father is a tailor, and lives in church-street, soho. on the 9th of january, about eleven o’clock at night, i stopped at the star and crown public-house, westminster, and left my coat over my horse’s head — i had a chaise standing at the door; i saw the prisoner go out, and suspected him — i went out, and missed my coat.
henry betts, a constable, had taken kerr in charge for another offence; two other witnesses did not appear. not guilty. second middlesex jury, before mr recorder.

john henry kolbe, baptised at westminster on 29 july 1800 — one of the eight sons, and eighteen years old on the night he lost his coat. he died on 13 april 1832, aged thirty-two, and was buried in the german lutheran register.
his younger brother george augustus sailed for algoa bay the following year. this is the closest thing this archive has to a voice from the house he left.

the rate books put his father at church street south, st anne’s soho in 1811, 1819, 1828 and 1831. the son says the same street, in 1819, under oath, to a court that had no interest in where he lived.
two sources with nothing whatever to do with each other — a parish tax list and a criminal indictment — agreeing on an address the family tree had wrong twice.
and what it shows of them

a coat worth six pounds — several months’ wages for a labourer, and exactly what a master tailor’s son would be wearing. a chaise and a horse at eleven at night outside a westminster public house. “my father is a tailor”, said plainly, twenty-five years before an obituary preferred esq.

how it was found, which is the part worth repeating. not by searching the old bailey. it came out of a surname sweep of findmypast for kolbe in london, in a list of 154 rows that was mostly rate books, where two entries said old bailey court records and were nearly scrolled past. the trial text itself is free, at oldbaileyonline.org, and always was. the rate books →

an eleventh child, and the only one with a birth date as well as a baptism date. louisa maria, born 13 may 1810, baptised 4 july, father john gottlob, mother mary. she sits in the 1808–1812 gap, and she is not in the familysearch index at all.
and three of them married
elizabeth kolbe married john milne in 1817 at st clement danes, both of that parish. she was twenty-one.

john henry kolbe married matilda ford on 26 april 1819 at st margaret, westminster, both of that parish. he was eighteen, and three months earlier he had been in the old bailey losing a six-pound coat. the trial →
jane day kolbe married in 1853 in the city of london — gro index, 1853 q3, vol am, 1170, p.33. the youngest of the eleven, and she lived to thirty-four at least.
a grandchild, probably
mary ann maria ford kolbe married at whitechapel in the first quarter of 1847 — gro index vol az, 840, p.16.

“ford” is matilda’s maiden name, carried as a forename in the way families did carry them, and there is no other ford anywhere near this family. she is very probably john henry and matilda’s daughter, born after the 1819 marriage and married fifteen years after her father died.
that is an inference from a forename and it is written down as one. the certificate would settle it, and it has not been ordered.
1807–1832 · seven kolbe burials in a german lutheran register, and two wives called mary

the 1844 obituary of george augustus kolbe calls him “the last remaining of eight sons of john godloff kolbe esq.” seven brothers died before december 1844 and this archive had never found one of them. it had guessed where to look — the german lutheran church of the savoy, tna series rg 4 — and had never been able to get at the registers. they are on findmypast, and they hold seven kolbes.

six rows, seven records: the 1807 child is entered twice, once in rg 4/4631 and once in rg 4/4630, with the same death date and the same age to the day. that is a register and its duplicate, not two children. rg 4/4630 was not on this archive’s list of savoy volumes.
matched against the baptisms, which were found the same afternoon
three brothers, dead and dated

charles samuel, baptised 3 february 1807 — dead at one year and ten days. frederick charles, baptised 12 march 1805 — dead at four years and six weeks. john henry, baptised 29 july 1800 — dead at thirty-two, on 13 april 1832, twelve years before the obituary that counted him.
and a sister with them: frederica carolina, baptised 18 august 1813, buried at eleven months.
two wives, and both of them mary

the archive had one mary and could not make her fit. there are two. the first died 2 august 1814 aged 46 — born about 1768, and buried a month after her eleven-month-old daughter. the second died 15 august 1824 aged 36 — born about 1788, and she is the mary named as mother at the 1819 baptism of jane day kolbe.
which is why a single mary would not work: she would have been bearing children from 1792 to 1819, and the woman who died in 1814 could not have been the mother in 1819.

what is still missing. three of the eight sons remain unnamed. the german lutheran baptism registers — rg 4/4627 and rg 4/4629 — are not on findmypast under any dataset name this archive could find, only the burials. the gaps in the westminster baptism run, 1808–1812 and 1814–1818, are where the other three sit.
1800–1845 · not brunswick square: a tailor rated in soho for thirty-one years

an 1844 obituary puts the family at brunswick-square. his own 1842 will and 1845 death put him in conduit street, off bond street. those are different parts of london and this archive could not choose between them. it has been waiting for a trade directory. what decided it was a rate book — the list of who paid the parish rates, house by house, year after year.

one hundred and twenty-one entries under twenty-four spellings of one forename. westminster rate books 1634–1900 index him as gothel, gotleb, gotleib, gotlieb, gotliel, gotlob, gotlobe, goltief, gottieb, gottiel, gottlieb, gottlob, gutlieb, kottieb, gilliet and — once — jos gottiel. a name search for “gottlieb” finds one entry in twenty-four. the run is only visible because the surname was searched and the forenames read.

the 1800 entry settles an older question too

this archive holds a line from a printed list of 234 master tailors who met over the combination act in december 1799: “kolbe, john, 18 broad-street, soho”. it had no way to test it. the rate book for 1800 puts a john kolbe in broad street north. two sources, neither aware of the other, one street.
and what it does to brunswick square

brunswick square is in bloomsbury. it is not in westminster and would not appear in any of these books, so they cannot disprove it. what they can do is close the gap: he is rated in soho from 1800 to 1831, he is in the 1841 census at st george hanover square with amelia a, charlotte and marianne kolbe, and he dies in st george hanover square in 1845. there is no window left for a bloomsbury house. conduit street is in st george hanover square. the obituary is the odd one out.

what a rate book is, and why it beat the directory. a trade directory lists the men who paid to be listed. a rate book lists everyone the parish could get money out of, every year, by street. this archive spent a fortnight trying to get at a london directory of the 1820s past google books’ quota and hathitrust’s bot check. the answer was in a tax record, which nobody thinks of as a genealogical source because it has no names of relatives in it. it has something better: an address, repeated thirty-one times.
september 2026 · four things findmypast does not have, and the controls that prove it

a month’s full subscription was opened on 16 september. four of the questions put to it came back empty. a nil return is worthless until a control shows the search works, so each one below is published with the count that makes it mean something. the method →
first, the trap — and it is the kind that answers wrongly rather than emptily
findmypast indexes the 21st light dragoons under four different regiment strings, and they hold different war office series.
¦indexed as records series years
¦21st dragoons 342 wo 22, wo 23, wo 121 1801–1886
¦21st regt of light dragoons 128 wo 97 only 1793–1813
¦21st light dragoons 66 wo 22, wo 23, wo 76 1801–1877

searching the obvious string alone would have produced a negative against an index holding no wo 97 at all — and wo 97, the chelsea discharge papers, is the series that would give james mountjoy his parish and county of birth.
1 · james mountjoy is not there
all four strings swept in full: 1,110 records. no mountjoy, montjoy, monjoy, mountjoye or montjoie in any of them.

the controls. wo 23/136, the 1806–07 volume, holds 18 men of the regiment, mark allen to jno warnsnop. wo 23/147, 1817–26, holds 12. the wo 97 run holds 128, 1793 to 1813. the alphabetical run through the ms goes martin, mcclay, mccracken, mccue, mcgregor, mcnary, merrick, morgan, morris, morrison — and in the other sweep, moses straight to napier.
eighteen pre-1860 mountjoys do exist in the set and every one is 36th, 44th or 60th foot.

and the wo 97 half of it is as strong as a negative can be made. that string resolves to “wo 97 — chelsea pensioners british army service records 1760–1913”, which is the exact series this archive named as the answer to question 12. its 128 men of the regiment are indexed with birth parish, birth town, birth county, birth country, age at attestation and date of attestation. they attested between 1793 and 1813, and the distribution peaks precisely where james mountjoy’s would fall — 35 in 1800, 25 in 1799, 10 in 1801, 9 in 1805. they were born in england (95), ireland (26), scotland (2), wales (2), and one each in switzerland, germany and unspecified great britain.

so the sentence this archive has been waiting to write is available for a hundred and twenty-eight other men and not for him. wo 97 before 1855 holds only soldiers discharged to a pension. a man who left the ranks at the cape without one, and stayed to make saddles, is exactly the man it would not hold.
2 · margaret downing has no london baptism
her burgersdorp gravestone says born london, 23 february 1803.

the controls. london baptisms 1801–1807 under the surname downing: 28 — louisa three times, eliza three times, susanna delafield, frances, robert, eliza eleanor, jacobus, joannes, george philip thomas, dennis, hugh robt., joseph, louisa towgood twice, thomas, william, samuel and the rest. no margaret in 1803. westminster’s own registers 1798–1810: 14 downing baptisms, and again no margaret. the set holds 239 downings in westminster overall.

a margaret downing does turn up in the roman catholic banns of st patrick’s, soho square, two streets from the kolbes’ own door — but the date is 22 september 1861 and the groom is henry shea. not her, and written down so that she does not become her later.
3 · the yorkshire half of question 6 does not exist
one profile welds a farmer of bilsdale, christened 1796 and buried at st hilda’s on 3 january 1853, to a john barry who died at de bruins poort in the cape on 8 january 1853 — five days later.

the controls. findmypast’s yorkshire burials includes bilsdale, st hilda, from the ryedale family history society transcripts, with burials at 1849, 1851, 1857, 1859 and on through the 1860s — january 1853 sits inside an indexed run.

a man buried at st hilda’s on 3 january 1853 is not in an index of 5,934 bilsdale burials, while 771 barrys are buried elsewhere in the same county. the surname is not invisible to the index. that profile has nothing under its english half.
4 · no cork baptism for a barry born to a neagle

john augustus barry’s 1903 death registration, made by a son who was in the room, answers irishman born in ireland and gives his mother only as “born neagle”. the family says county cork. he was 84 years 2 months, so born about november 1818.

the controls. irish roman catholic baptisms in cork for 1818 alone: 12,273. john barry baptisms in cork, 1816 to 1820: 71. john barry baptisms in all ireland with a mother surnamed nagle: four — 1811, 1845, 1860, 1876. none between 1816 and 1820. under neagle or nagel: none at all.
the honest limit of this one: it tests the roman catholic registers. he may not have been catholic, and the church of ireland registers for cork largely burnt in the four courts in 1922.

and a citation of this archive’s own that does not resolve. this site has been carrying r_177176049779 for petrus jacobus booysen’s 1812 birth — a findmypast transcript reference recorded once, from a search run without a subscription, and never seen. opened twice on a live full subscription, it returns a 500 error from findmypast’s own transcript page. it does not open. a reference cited and unread is exactly what this archive corrects other people for. corrections →

basutoland records (1883), p. 436. frans johannes cornelis cronje , sworn at smithfield on 14 september 1858 : hunting in june 1831 , “we then met with the missionaries kolbe and klerk with some bushmen at bethulie.” “klerk” is almost certainly james clark , and the pairing is what identifies the kolbe. testimony taken to argue the land had been empty.

moodie, battles and adventures (1888), p. 93. “a report from commandant j. g. e. kolbe to commandant botha, dated platberg, 2nd nov., 1867” — a document the commandant wrote, summarised and not printed. the paragraph above it is the rev. mr jousse on a raid where women and children were killed; the juxtaposition is moodie’s, not the record’s , and both are left on the page.

hofstede, geschiedenis van den oranje-vrijstaat (1876), p. 232. “ik bedoel den kommandant van bloemfontein j. g. e. kolbe” — taken by a fatal fever, 4 april 1868 , “niet op ’t bed van eer, maar in het midden zijner betrekkingen” . it names his seat , which this archive did not have. the obituary’s 3 april stands: it was a friday and his twenty-fifth wedding anniversary.

the same book, p. 160 — and this one withdrew a find. three men were allowed to bring away louw wepener’s bones on 6 april 1866, and one is “jan colbe” . this archive’s commandant is jan gersem eliezer kolbe, so the page was fetched rather than reasoned about. the type says colbe , in a book that sets kolbe seventeen times. nothing was taken.

/dna/.title: The DNA — The Booyzen Archive
blocks: two kits, read 16 september 2026

two descendants of this line have tested. what they say about the cape — the cousinhood counted, the families that keep arriving out of strangers' trees, and a trace of ancestry this archive has not written down before.

on privacy, first. both testers are living. neither is named here and neither is described beyond her position in the descent. the figures kept below are the ones that bear on people long dead. everything else is held privately. method →

where this came from. two kits belonging to descendants of this line, read at myheritage and at 23andme. the work was done in the lerena archive, because the tester's father was a lerena; everything on this page is the half of it that belongs here. the lerena archive was asking whether a chromosome could reach an argentine great-grandfather. it mostly could not — but the same two kits are loud about the cape, and that half of the answer belongs here.
the two kits, and why the aunt is the valuable one
a great-great-granddaughter of the booyzen line, through her mother.
she is roughly half of this family. her father's side is argentine and english, which is what makes her useful here: anything cape in her can only have come through her mother.
kit two — the instrument
her mother's sister - an aunt, on this line and no other.
2,035.27 cm shared with her niece — 29.94%, across 39 at 23andme, 41 at myheritage.

she is the instrument. she carries this family's dna and none of the argentine or english. any match shared with her is cape; any match absent from her list is not. that subtraction has now been run - see the aunt's own chart below - and it worked.
the cousinhood, counted

23andme asks every tester which countries their grandparents were born in. it is a field they fill in themselves, not an inference from where they live. across the 1,500 closest genetic relatives of the younger kit, twenty countries are named.
name at least one grandparent born in south africa

of the twenty countries named across 1,500 relatives, south africa is first by a factor of four, and more than half of those name all four grandparents there. this is what a cape family looks like from the inside. the next countries down are the shape of the diaspora rather than of the family — the united states 144, great britain 135, and then zimbabwe, namibia and the netherlands in the tens.
and the surnames those relatives carry
the facet shows the top twenty only. it cannot be used to say any surname is absent.
this archive’s own spine, arriving out of strangers’ trees
myheritage computes a documented path between two trees where it can find one — a theory of family relativity. it is not a guess from centimorgans; it is two pedigrees meeting at a named couple.
500 matches carry a computed relationship path
every one of the ten largest theories lands in this family. booyzen, barry and kolbe appear together, which is this archive's own spine arriving unprompted out of somebody else's tree.

the surnames those theories name, in order of the size of the match: booyzen, booysen, barry, kolbe, kruger, venter, nel, basson, louw, pretorius, botha, jordaan, du toit, de villiers, olivier, visser, malan.

booyzen, barry and kolbe appear together, repeatedly, in trees kept by people this family has never heard of. that is not new information about the descent — those three names are the spine this archive was built on, and they were established from registers. it is something better: independent confirmation, from the other direction, that the three lines really do sit together where this archive puts them. the barrys → · the kolbes →
fourteen ancestral couples, sorted for you

myheritage autoclusters, generated 15 september 2026. the tool groups a tester's dna matches into blocks that all match each other as well as the tester, so each block is in practice the descendants of one ancestral couple. it was run on the niece's kit.

fourteen clusters, 107 matches, from 50.6 cm upward. every single one of them is cape afrikaner or british isles. this is the most concrete thing in the whole dna file for this archive: fourteen ancestral couples, sorted for you, out of a database rather than out of a register.

start with cluster 7. cluster 7 is the one to start on - six matches from 56 to 333 cm, the largest match on the whole chart among them, carrying butler, daniel and daschner. those are the trees in which booyzen, booysen and barry appear together as ancestral surnames. the barrys →

and why the fourteen can be trusted. the niece's son was clustered on the same night as a control. his father is a defranceski of istria, and his chart throws up two plainly croatian clusters - butorac, pavelich, jagustin, krkljes, racic, glas - beside the cape ones. so the tool demonstrably separates a foreign paternal line from this family's when both are present. the fourteen cape clusters on his mother's chart are not an artefact of the method.
each cluster is a couple this archive either already has or does not. take them one at a time, open the trees, and find where they join the spine. fourteen leads, each one already proved to be blood.
the aunt’s own chart — the purest one in the family
the aunt was clustered too, on 15 september 2026. hers is the purest chart in the family for this archive's purposes: she is on this line and no other, so every cluster on it is cape by construction.
¦1 71 75.3–158.3 ackermann, andre, attwell, brits, calitz, carons, carrick, coetsee, coetzee, crossey
¦2 6 77.5–194.1 daschner, du-plessis, kotze, labuschagne, pistorius
¦3 6 76.3–319.4 daniel, dreyers-in-south-africa, gambale, smith
¦4 5 80–203.7 andrews, bailie, de-jager, lotter, randall
¦5 4 89.7–143.1 butler, duncan, martin-hardy-ellis, mulder
¦6 4 94.2–110.4 faraday, johnson, lightcap, priceglendinning

and the shape of it is a finding in itself. cluster 1 is enormous - 71 of her 98 clustered matches, from 75 to 158 cm, carrying ackermann, andre, attwell, brits, calitz, carons, carrick, coetsee and more. a single block of seventy-one is not one couple; it is a densely intermarried community, which is exactly what the eighteenth and nineteenth century cape was. splitting it is a job for a tighter threshold.

her chart was used as the instrument in the lerena archive: subtract it from her niece's and what is left is the niece's father's side. it worked, and the one paternal cluster it found turned out to be english rather than argentine. the method and its trap - a floor mismatch that nearly produced four false positives - are written up there. how that went →
a trace this archive has not written down before
this is the one finding here that is genuinely new, and it should be read carefully rather than quickly.
northern indian & pakistani

small, and real. west central african and south asian together, at trace level, is the ordinary genetic signature of the eighteenth-century cape - the household slavery the colony ran on, written into the families that came out of it. in the niece these are halved by her argentine and english father, so in her mother they are roughly double, and further back they are larger again.

and the care it needs. a trace figure at half a percent is at the edge of what any panel can call, and this archive is not going to convert it into a named ancestor. it is recorded because it is consistent, because it is where this family lived, and because leaving it out would be a choice as much as putting it in.

it is also worth saying plainly why it can be attributed to this side at all. the younger tester’s other two grandparents are argentine and english. neither an english devon family nor a río de la plata one produces a south asian trace. the cape does, constantly, and it is where this family has been since the eighteenth century.

what would turn this from a trace into a person. 23andme will assign each slice of ancestry to one parent or the other. it is behind a paid tier and this archive does not buy sources — but one screen would put these two figures definitively on this side of the family rather than on inference. it is on the work list.
what has not been done
cluster 1 on the aunt's chart holds 71 of her 98 matches in one block. that is the cape marrying itself, not one couple. re-running at a tighter threshold should break it into something usable.
23andme's parental inheritance, which would put the cape trace definitively on this side, is behind a paid tier.
nobody has yet taken the fourteen clusters one at a time and found where each joins the spine.

the first of those is the one that matters. the aunt is on this line and no other. subtract her match list from her niece’s and what remains is argentine and english; keep only what they share and what remains is this family, several thousand people deep, sorted for free. nobody has run it yet.
where the other half of this went

the same two kits are written up from the other side in the lerena archive, where the question is an argentine great-grandfather rather than a cape one, and where the answer is a good deal less comfortable than it is here.

/disputed/.title: Disputed — The Booyzen Archive
blocks: twenty-three problems — ten of them now solved

the myheritage tree behind this archive is unusually well sourced and, in places, impossible. rather than quietly choosing the readings that suit, this page lists every contradiction found — including the ones that damage the family's own story.
why this page exists first, not last

a family tree that shows no contradictions has usually had them removed. this one has not. it carries myheritage's own consistency warnings, several conflicting birth facts, two canadian and english census records attached to people who were in the karoo, and at least one profile that is demonstrably two different men fused together.
every one of them is listed here. three classes are used:

fatal the record cannot be true as it stands and a link must be broken. serious a real conflict that changes a conclusion. reject an obvious wrong match or typing error, safely discarded. resolved settled by a document read in september 2026.

ten have now been settled, every one of them by reading scans the family tree had been carrying, untranscribed, for years. one confirmed a guess this archive had already written down; two showed that a researcher had gone out and photographed the wrong building; and one — the two gertrudes — turned out not to be an error at all. this archive has also had to correct two mistakes of its own. the documents →
¦person the contradiction class reading

¦anna maria van der merwe — whose daughter? the family tree makes her a daughter of david schalk van der merwe and anna elizabeth louw, born 1785. de villiers's printed cape genealogy of 1893, volume 2, makes her a daughter of willem van der merwe and hester maria van der merwe, baptised 5 october 1788 — fourteen days after the man she married. both cannot be right. serious neither is being adopted, and the interesting part is that it does not matter to the conclusion the archive drew from her. on the tree's version david schalk is her father; on the book's he is her brother, baptised 10 october 1790. the name stands one step from her either way, and her son — baptised 4 january 1807 — is the only david schalk in the whole first volume of the cape genealogies, the volume holding every booijsen de villiers recorded. a conclusion that survives both readings of the evidence is the only kind worth keeping. what the disagreement does cost is her: she has two sets of parents and no way to choose, and the baptism register of 5 october 1788 at cape town would end it. →

¦gerthardus lodewikus booysen — did he exist? the 1876 rustenburg sterfkennis of petrus jacobus booijsen, notice 678, names his parents on line 3 as gerthardus lödewikus booijsen and magdalena de beer. de villiers (1893) and de villiers & pama (1981) both place that petrus jacobus under jan booijsen, b3c4. the mother agrees; the father does not. serious four things now point one way and the chart has not been moved. riël smit confirms from the 1981 revision — which this archive does not own — that petrus jacobus is still placed under jan. pieter van zyl searched for a marriage between a gerhardus lodewicus and a magdalena de beer and found none. jan was dead more than forty years before petrus jacobus died. and the disputed name sits nine lines lower on the same sheet: line 12 lists eight children and the fifth is jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen — so the name in the parents' box is the back half of a son's name, and the half that was dropped is jan. the man who signed was hendrik stefanus, the seventh child, born about 1828, writing the name of a grandfather dead before he was ten. the spine stays where it is on purpose: everything against him is a printed genealogy agreeing with its own earlier edition, which is one source agreeing with itself, and what he has is a primary document signed by a son. jan booijsen is entered as inferred. the baptism entry of 21 september 1788 ends it, and it is not on familysearch — that collection begins in 1843. →

¦stephanus francois booyzen (1874–1940) — whose son? this archive placed him as a son of petrus jacobus booysen and his second wife johanna margaritha pretorius, on his birth date alone — his own 1940 sterfkennis names neither parent, because his widow wrote only “oorlede” for both. the 1900 death notice of elizabetha margaretha marais names a stephanus francois booijzen as her son by david schalk booijzen, an unmarried major at pretoria in 1904 — and the 1874 man died at east lynne, pretoria. serious 13 september 2026, later: his own marriage register adds to the new reading without settling it. mosselbaai, 5 september 1905, certificate 1318 — he is thirty, a jonkman, a metselaar, and his woonplaas is pretoria; eleven weeks later david schalk booijzen of goede hoop, pretoria married again in that city. the 1900 notice calls david schalk's stephanus françois an unmarried major, which is exactly what this man was. but the register has no column for parents and no column for birthplace, so it cannot decide anything. and his own eleven children add a third point. his 1940 estate names them, and the eldest is david schalk booyzen. if he is david schalk booijzen’s son, that boy is called after his grandfather outright; under the reading this archive published, he is called after a great-uncle. two of the eleven — ewert philippus and susanna fredrika aletta — are called straight after his wife’s parents, evert philip boshoff and susanna frederika aletta meyer, which shows this couple did name children after grandparents. the naming argues for the new reading: her father was stephanus francois marais, which is exactly where the forename would come from, and there is no stephanus francois anywhere in the pretorius side. but “serious”, not resolved — two men of one name in one town is precisely the mistake this archive keeps catching itself in, and the 1940 notice still names nobody. the inferred row stands, flagged, until a document settles it. →

¦anna maria van der merwe — married 1805 or 1825? the tree marries her to petrus jacobus booysen in 1805 at graaff-reinet and has her dead “before march 1825”. familysearch carries a dutch reformed marriage of petrus jacobus booÿzen and anna maria van der merwe dated 9 march 1825, at cape town, indexed three separate times. resolved resolved, 13 september 2026. a dutch reformed baptism names david schalk booijzen, born 12 december 1806, as the son of pieter jacobus booijzen and anna maria van der merwe — and he is first of the eight on the 1876 sterfkennis. they were married by 1806, so the 1805 marriage at graaff-reinet stands and the 1825 cape town record is a different couple of the same two very common names. it also rewrites the wall on the ancestor chart, which said “only a family tree puts her here”. it no longer does. what is still open is whether she is the mother of the 1812 man in the direct line; no document says so. the original note, kept: the tree's death date is “before march 1825” and the record is dated 9 march 1825. either the death date was derived from this very record by someone reading it as an end rather than a beginning, or the 1825 marriage is a different couple entirely — cape town is six hundred miles from graaff-reinet, and both names are common. the archive is not going to guess which. →

¦john barry (1796–1853) buried at st hilda's, bilsdale, yorkshire on 3 january 1853 — and dies at de bruins poort, eastern cape, on 8 january 1853, five days later. resolved resolved, 14 september 2026, and this page did not say so for three weeks. they are two men, and the yorkshire one was followed past the date the cape one died: the 1851 census has him at ship yards, ruswarp, whitby, aged 55, a ship owner — the only john barry of that age in the whole yorkshire census — and john barry deaths are registered in the whitby district in 1858 and 1860. he outlived the cape man by at least five years. the bilsdale burial does not exist either: findmypast indexes 5,934 bilsdale burials including the years either side of 1853, and not one barry among them. and the description was wrong too — “a yorkshire farmer of bilsdale” is the family tree’s phrase; the censuses show a whitby ship owner, and bilsdale is only the residence parish on his 1838 marriage licence. what remains is not a conflation but an absence: the cape man has no birth, no arrival and no burial, and the 1796 in the heading above belongs to the yorkshire man. his son’s 1903 registration says only an irishman, born in ireland. →

the one that matters most
"our great great grandfather was shot and killed by the british."
neither candidate fits, and one of them is now conclusively out.
petrus jacobus booysen died in 1884 — supported by a cape probate record. that is fifteen years before the war began. he is out.

willem hermanus booyzen died on 13 september 1905 at doorn street, indwe, of an ulcer of the stomach, after fourteen months of illness, attended by a doctor — three years after the war ended, in his own house, with his eldest son present. documented he was not shot by anybody. the death registration →
inferred three readings survive, and the archive does not choose between them:
the generations are miscounted. tersia booyzen was counting from herself, not from the current researcher. her "great great grandfather" may be a man this archive has not identified.
"shot and killed" is not an execution. it may mean killed in action, or shot during a farm clearance — neither of which would appear on the treason lists.
the story belongs to a collateral booysen, not to the direct line at all — which the testimony half-concedes when it distinguishes rebels from joiners within the same surname.
all three are checkable. forty-four cape colonists were executed for high treason, and that list is closed. what would settle it →
what is not in dispute

it is worth ending on this. the direct descent itself is unbroken and well sourced from gerthardus lodewikus booysen to david defranceski. the contradictions above sit on side branches, spouses' records and dates of death — not on the parent-to-child links of the line. nothing on this page moves anybody out of the family.
